## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lecture, you will be able to:
- Explain why brute-force alignment is impractical for modern sequencing data
- Distinguish between mapping and alignment
- Build and search substring indexes
- Understand hash functions and hash tables in the context of genomics
- Describe how BLAST uses word lookup tables to accelerate homology search
- Construct and search tries and suffix tries
- Explain the relationship between suffix tries, suffix trees, and suffix arrays
- Perform the Burrows-Wheeler Transform and understand its properties
- Describe how the FM index enables fast, memory-efficient sequence search
- Compare and contrast Bowtie2 and BWA-MEM alignment strategies

## 1. Introduction: The Challenge of Large Datasets

Modern sequencing instruments produce staggering volumes of data. An Illumina NovaSeq 6000 can generate **up to 20 billion reads** in a single run. Each of those reads must be placed onto a reference genome -- for humans, that means searching through **$3 \times 10^9$ base pairs**.

### Why Dynamic Programming Fails at Scale

In earlier lectures we learned about dynamic programming alignment algorithms like Smith-Waterman and Needleman-Wunsch. These are beautiful algorithms, but they have a critical limitation: **time complexity**.

For a single pairwise alignment of a read of length $m$ against a reference of length $n$:

$$T = O(mn)$$

This is fine for comparing two sequences. But what happens at genome scale?

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Reference genome length ($n$) | $3 \times 10^9$ bp (human) |
| Number of reads ($d$) | $20 \times 10^9$ (NovaSeq run) |
| Average read length ($m$) | 150 bp |
| Total operations | $d \times m \times n$ |

Let's compute the total number of operations:

$$d \times m \times n = 20 \times 10^9 \times 150 \times 3 \times 10^9 = 9 \times 10^{21}$$

That is **9 sextillion operations**. Even at $10^9$ operations per second per CPU core, this would require:

$$\frac{9 \times 10^{21}}{10^9 \times 3.15 \times 10^7} \approx 285,000 \text{ CPU-years}$$

On a cluster of 1,000 CPUs, this would still take **over 285 years**. Clearly, we cannot align every read against the entire genome using dynamic programming.

:::{.callout-important}
## Key Insight
We need a fundamentally different strategy. Instead of comparing every read against every position in the genome, we need a way to *jump directly* to the most promising locations. This is the idea behind **indexing**.
:::

The rest of this lecture traces the intellectual journey from simple indexes to the sophisticated data structures used by modern aligners like Bowtie2 and BWA-MEM.

:::{.callout-note}
## Roadmap
Here is the path we will follow -- each step motivated by limitations of the previous one:

| Step | Data Structure / Tool | Limitation it addresses |
|:----:|----------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | **Brute Force** | *(baseline -- too slow)* |
| 2 | **Substring Index** | *(fixed k, many false hits)* |
| 3 | **Hash Tables** | *(fast lookup for k-mers)* |
| 4 | **BLAST** | *(word lookup + extend -- fast homology search)* |
| 5 | **Tries** | *(tree-based prefix lookup)* |
| 6 | **Suffix Trie** | *(any-length query, but O(n²) space)* |
| 7 | **Suffix Tree** | *(linear space, but 47 GB for human)* |
| 8 | **Suffix Array** | *(12 GB, simpler)* |
| 9 | **BWT** | *(compressible and searchable)* |
| 10 | **FM Index** | *(~1.25 GB, fast search)* |
| 11 | **Bowtie2 / BWA-MEM** | *(practical tools you will use)* |
:::

## 2. Mapping vs. Alignment

Before diving into indexing, let's clarify two terms that are often confused.

The tools we will study in this lecture were shaped by a handful of researchers. [Heng Li](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heng_Li), a student of [Richard Durbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Durbin_(scientist)), created BWA, SAMtools, and minimap2 -- his tools are used in virtually every genomics study published today. [Ben Langmead](https://www.langmead-lab.org/), a student of [Steven Salzberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Salzberg), developed Bowtie and Bowtie2, among the most widely cited alignment tools in history. And [Webb Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webb_Miller) pioneered the foundational sequence alignment algorithms (including BLASTZ and multiz) that made comparative genomics possible. You will encounter their work throughout this lecture.

Heng Li provides a useful distinction between two terms that are often confused:

| Concept | Definition | Goal |
|---------|-----------|------|
| **Mapping** | Determining the most likely genomic region a read originates from | Find the *location* |
| **Alignment** | Determining the base-by-base correspondence between read and reference | Find the *exact placement* |

**Mapping** is like determining that your sequence likely came from chromosome 17. **Alignment** is determining the exact base-pair coordinates (e.g., chr17:7,668,402-7,668,551) and finding that there is a G>A substitution at position 120 of the read.

In practice, most tools do both: they first **map** (find candidate locations using an index) and then **align** (perform local alignment at those locations). This two-phase approach -- often called **seed-and-extend** -- is the foundation of nearly all modern read aligners.

## 3. Indexing with Substrings

### The Inverted Index Concept

Think about the index at the back of a book. When you want to find where "transcription" is discussed, you don't read the entire book -- you look up the word in the index, which tells you the page numbers. This is an **inverted index**: given a term, it returns the locations where that term appears.

We can apply the same idea to DNA sequences:

- **Forward index**: Given a position, what substring is there? (This is just the genome itself.)
- **Inverted index**: Given a substring, where does it occur? (This is what we need for mapping.)

### Building an Index from Substrings

To create an index from a text $T$, we:

1. **Extract** all substrings of a fixed length $L$ (these are called **L-mers** or **k-mers**)
2. **Record** each substring along with the position where it occurs
3. **Organize** these entries so that lookups are fast

For example, with text `CGTGCCTACTTACTTACAT` and $L = 5$:

| Position | 5-mer |
|----------|-------|
| 0 | CGTGC |
| 1 | GTGCC |
| 2 | TGCCT |
| 3 | GCCTA |
| ... | ... |

### Searching the Index

To find where a pattern $P$ occurs:

1. Extract a substring of length $L$ from $P$
2. Look it up in the index to get candidate positions
3. **Extend** the match at each candidate position to verify the full pattern

### Trade-offs

The choice of $L$ (substring length) and the interval between extracted substrings involve trade-offs:

| Parameter | Larger value | Smaller value |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| Substring length $L$ | More specific (fewer false hits), more memory | Less specific (more false hits), less memory |
| Extraction interval | Faster indexing, less memory, may miss some matches | Slower indexing, more memory, more complete |

### Specificity in Practice

How unique are k-mers in real genomes? Here are approximate numbers for human chromosome 1 (about 249 Mb):

| k-mer length | Unique k-mers | % of possible | Average occurrences |
|--------------|--------------|---------------|-------------------|
| 8 | 65,536 | 100% | ~3,800 |
| 10 | 1,048,372 | 99.97% | ~238 |
| 12 | 16,543,411 | 98.5% | ~15 |
| 14 | 175,891,774 | 65.5% | ~1.4 |
| 16 | 237,533,060 | 5.5% | ~1.05 |

Notice that even with 16-mers, only about 5.5% of possible 16-mers appear, but almost every one that does appear is unique. This means longer k-mers give us very specific index hits. This is why most aligners use seed lengths of at least 16-22 bp -- shorter seeds produce too many spurious hits, overwhelming the extension phase.

```{=html}
    <input id="si-pattern" type="text" value="TACTTAC" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />

<div style="display:flex; gap:8px; margin-bottom:12px;">
  <button id="si-build" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Build Index</button>

  <button id="si-reset" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#9E9E9E; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Reset</button>
</div>
<div id="si-text-display" style="font-family:monospace; font-size:1.3em; padding:10px; background:#f5f5f5; border-radius:4px; margin-bottom:10px; letter-spacing:2px; overflow-x:auto; white-space:nowrap;"></div>
<div id="si-index-table" style="max-height:300px; overflow-y:auto; margin-bottom:10px;"></div>
<div id="si-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; min-height:40px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
  let index = {};

  function buildIndex() {
    const text = $('si-text').value.toUpperCase();
    const L = parseInt($('si-length').value);
    const interval = parseInt($('si-interval').value);
    index = {};
    const display = $('si-text-display');
    display.innerHTML = text.split('').map((c, i) =>
      `<span id="si-c-${i}" style="display:inline-block;width:1.1em;text-align:center;">${c}</span>`
    ).join('');

    for (let i = 0; i <= text.length - L; i += interval) {
      const sub = text.substring(i, i + L);
      if (!index[sub]) index[sub] = [];
      index[sub].push(i);
    }

    let html = '<table style="width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:0.85em;">';
    html += '<tr style="background:#2196F3;color:white;"><th style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:left;">Substring</th><th style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:left;">Positions</th></tr>';
    const sorted = Object.keys(index).sort();
    sorted.forEach((key, i) => {
      const bg = i % 2 === 0 ? '#f9f9f9' : '#fff';
      html += `<tr id="si-row-${key}" style="background:${bg};"><td style="padding:4px 8px;font-family:monospace;">${key}</td><td style="padding:4px 8px;">${index[key].join(', ')}</td></tr>`;
    });
    html += '</table>';
    $('si-index-table').innerHTML = html;
    $('si-log').innerHTML = `<strong>Index built!</strong> Extracted ${sorted.length} unique ${L}-mers from text of length ${text.length} (interval=${interval}).`;
  }

  function searchPattern() {
    const text = $('si-text').value.toUpperCase();
    const pattern = $('si-pattern').value.toUpperCase();
    const L = parseInt($('si-length').value);
    if (Object.keys(index).length === 0) { buildIndex(); }

    // Reset highlights
    for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
      const el = document.getElementById(`si-c-${i}`);
      if (el) el.style.background = 'none';
    }
    document.querySelectorAll('[id^="si-row-"]').forEach(r => r.style.background = '');

    if (pattern.length < L) {
      $('si-log').innerHTML = `<span style="color:#f44336;">Pattern must be at least ${L} characters long (the substring length).</span>`;
      return;
    }

    const queryMer = pattern.substring(0, L);
    const rowEl = document.getElementById(`si-row-${queryMer}`);
    if (rowEl) rowEl.style.background = '#FF9800';

    const candidates = index[queryMer] || [];
    let log = `<strong>Searching for:</strong> <code>${pattern}</code><br>`;
    log += `<strong>Query ${L}-mer:</strong> <code>${queryMer}</code> &rarr; `;

    if (candidates.length === 0) {
      log += `<span style="color:#f44336;">Not found in index. No matches.</span>`;
      $('si-log').innerHTML = log;
      return;
    }

    log += `Found at positions: ${candidates.join(', ')}<br><strong>Verification:</strong><br>`;
    let matches = [];
    candidates.forEach(pos => {
      const sub = text.substring(pos, pos + pattern.length);
      if (sub === pattern) {
        matches.push(pos);
        for (let j = pos; j < pos + pattern.length && j < text.length; j++) {
          const el = document.getElementById(`si-c-${j}`);
          if (el) el.style.background = '#4CAF50';
        }
        log += `&nbsp;&nbsp;Position ${pos}: <code>${sub}</code> = <code>${pattern}</code> <span style="color:#4CAF50;">&#10004; Match!</span><br>`;
      } else {
        for (let j = pos; j < pos + pattern.length && j < text.length; j++) {
          const el = document.getElementById(`si-c-${j}`);
          if (el && el.style.background !== 'rgb(76, 175, 80)') el.style.background = '#ffcdd2';
        }
        log += `&nbsp;&nbsp;Position ${pos}: <code>${sub}</code> &ne; <code>${pattern}</code> <span style="color:#f44336;">&#10008; Mismatch</span><br>`;
      }
    });
    log += `<strong>Result: ${matches.length} match(es)</strong> at position(s): ${matches.join(', ') || 'none'}`;
    $('si-log').innerHTML = log;
  }

  $('si-build').addEventListener('click', buildIndex);
  $('si-search').addEventListener('click', searchPattern);
  $('si-reset').addEventListener('click', () => {
    index = {};
    $('si-text-display').innerHTML = '';
    $('si-index-table').innerHTML = '';
    $('si-log').innerHTML = '';
  });
  buildIndex();
})();
</script>
```

## 4. Hashing and Hash Functions

Before we go further with indexing, we need to understand a fundamental computer science concept that underlies fast lookups: **hashing**. If you have never taken a computer science course, don't worry -- the idea is intuitive once you see it.

### What is a Hash Function?

Imagine you work in a library and need to file thousands of books so you can find any one instantly. One strategy: assign each book to a numbered shelf based on a simple rule applied to its title. For example, "count the letters in the title and take the remainder when dividing by 100." Book titles with 312 letters go to shelf 12 (since 312 mod 100 = 12).

A **hash function** is exactly this kind of rule. It takes an input (of any size) and converts it to a fixed-size number:

$$h: \text{input} \rightarrow \text{integer in range } [0, N)$$

### Properties of Good Hash Functions

| Property | What it means | Why it matters |
|----------|--------------|----------------|
| **Deterministic** | Same input always gives same output | You can find things again! |
| **Uniform distribution** | Outputs are spread evenly across the range | No shelf gets overcrowded |
| **Fast to compute** | O(1) or O(k) for k-length input | The whole point is speed |

### How Hash Tables Work

A **hash table** (also called a hash map or dictionary) uses a hash function to create a fast lookup structure:

1. Create an array of $N$ "buckets"
2. To **store** a key-value pair: compute $h(\text{key})$, put the pair in that bucket
3. To **retrieve** a value: compute $h(\text{key})$, go directly to that bucket

The result? **O(1) average-case lookup** -- constant time regardless of how many items are stored. Compare this to searching a sorted list ($O(\log n)$) or an unsorted list ($O(n)$).

### A Simple DNA Hash Function

For DNA k-mers, we can convert each base to a 2-bit number:

| Base | Binary |
|------|--------|
| A | 00 |
| C | 01 |
| G | 10 |
| T | 11 |

Since we use 2 bits per base, each position can hold 4 values (A=0, C=1, G=2, T=3). We can read a k-mer as a **base-4 number** to get a unique integer. For a 3-mer, the first base is multiplied by $4^2 = 16$, the second by $4^1 = 4$, and the third by $4^0 = 1$:

$$h(\text{ACG}) = 0 \times 4^2 + 1 \times 4^1 + 2 \times 4^0 = 0 + 4 + 2 = 6$$

This is perfect for DNA because it maps every possible k-mer to a unique integer (for small k), and it is extremely fast to compute.

### Collisions

What happens when two different keys hash to the same bucket? This is called a **collision**. For our library analogy, two books with titles of the same length get assigned to the same shelf.

Common collision resolution strategies:

- **Chaining**: Each bucket holds a linked list of all items that hash there
- **Open addressing**: If a bucket is full, try the next one (linear probing)

With a good hash function and a large enough table, collisions are rare and lookups remain fast.

### Why This Matters for Genomics

Hash tables are everywhere in bioinformatics:

- **K-mer counting** (jellyfish, KMC): hash each k-mer, increment its count
- **Sequence indexing** (BLAST): hash seed words for fast lookup
- **Genome assembly** (de Bruijn graphs): hash k-mers to find overlaps
- **Minimizers**: hash k-mers to select representative seeds

```{=html}

<div id="viz-hash-table" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Interactive Hash Table Demo</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">Type DNA k-mers to see them hashed and placed in buckets. Watch collisions happen!</p>

  <div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">K-mer to insert:</label>
    <input id="ht-kmer" type="text" value="ACG" maxlength="6" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; text-transform:uppercase; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <div style="min-width:120px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Table size:</label>
    <input id="ht-size" type="number" value="8" min="4" max="16" style="width:80px; padding:6px; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="ht-insert" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer; height:36px;">Insert</button>
  <button id="ht-batch" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#FF9800; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer; height:36px;">Batch Insert (random)</button>
  <button id="ht-clear" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#9E9E9E; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer; height:36px;">Clear</button>
</div>
<div id="ht-calc" style="padding:8px; background:#e3f2fd; border-radius:4px; font-family:monospace; font-size:0.9em; margin-bottom:10px; min-height:24px;"></div>
<svg id="ht-svg" width="100%" height="320" style="border:1px solid #eee; border-radius:4px; background:#fafafa;"></svg>
<div id="ht-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; margin-top:10px; min-height:30px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
  const baseVal = {A:0, C:1, G:2, T:3};
  let tableSize = 8;
  let buckets = [];
  let collisionCount = 0;

  function hashKmer(kmer) {
    let h = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < kmer.length; i++) {
      h = h * 4 + (baseVal[kmer[i]] || 0);
    }
    return h % tableSize;
  }

  function initTable() {
    tableSize = parseInt($('ht-size').value) || 8;
    buckets = Array.from({length: tableSize}, () => []);
    collisionCount = 0;
    render();
    $('ht-log').innerHTML = '';
    $('ht-calc').innerHTML = '';
  }

  function render() {
    const svg = $('ht-svg');
    const w = svg.clientWidth || 860;
    const bucketW = Math.min(100, (w - 40) / tableSize);
    const startX = (w - bucketW * tableSize) / 2;
    let html = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < tableSize; i++) {
      const x = startX + i * bucketW;
      html += `<rect x="${x}" y="40" width="${bucketW - 4}" height="40" fill="#e3f2fd" stroke="#2196F3" rx="4"/>`;
      html += `<text x="${x + bucketW/2 - 2}" y="65" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1565C0">${i}</text>`;
      buckets[i].forEach((kmer, j) => {
        const yy = 95 + j * 32;
        const color = j === 0 ? '#4CAF50' : '#FF9800';
        html += `<rect x="${x}" y="${yy}" width="${bucketW - 4}" height="28" fill="${color}" rx="4"/>`;
        html += `<text x="${x + bucketW/2 - 2}" y="${yy + 19}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-family="monospace" fill="white" font-weight="bold">${kmer}</text>`;
      });
    }
    html += `<text x="${w/2}" y="20" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#666">Hash Table Buckets (size=${tableSize}) | Collisions: ${collisionCount}</text>`;
    svg.innerHTML = html;
  }

  function insertKmer(kmer) {
    kmer = kmer.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, '');
    if (kmer.length === 0) return;
    const h = hashKmer(kmer);
    let calcStr = kmer.split('').map((c, i) => {
      const power = kmer.length - 1 - i;
      return `${baseVal[c]}x4<sup>${power}</sup>`;
    }).join(' + ');
    let rawVal = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < kmer.length; i++) rawVal = rawVal * 4 + (baseVal[kmer[i]] || 0);
    calcStr += ` = ${rawVal} mod ${tableSize} = <strong>${h}</strong>`;
    $('ht-calc').innerHTML = `h(${kmer}) = ${calcStr}`;

    if (buckets[h].length > 0) {
      collisionCount++;
      $('ht-log').innerHTML = `<span style="color:#FF9800;"><strong>Collision!</strong> Bucket ${h} already has [${buckets[h].join(', ')}]. Adding ${kmer} via chaining.</span>`;
    } else {
      $('ht-log').innerHTML = `Inserted <strong>${kmer}</strong> into bucket ${h}.`;
    }
    buckets[h].push(kmer);
    render();
  }

  function batchInsert() {
    const bases = 'ACGT';
    const k = 3;
    for (let n = 0; n < 6; n++) {
      let kmer = '';
      for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) kmer += bases[Math.floor(Math.random() * 4)];
      insertKmer(kmer);
    }
  }

  initTable();
  $('ht-insert').addEventListener('click', () => insertKmer($('ht-kmer').value));
  $('ht-kmer').addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') insertKmer($('ht-kmer').value); });
  $('ht-batch').addEventListener('click', batchInsert);
  $('ht-clear').addEventListener('click', initTable);
  $('ht-size').addEventListener('change', initTable);
})();
</script>
```

## 5. How BLAST Works: Putting It All Together

In the previous lecture we learned about dynamic programming alignment (Smith-Waterman) and the seed-and-extend strategy used by LASTZ. Now let's look at **BLAST** (Basic Local Alignment Search Tool) -- arguably the most widely used program in all of biology -- and see how it combines indexing, lookup tables, and local alignment into a remarkably fast homology search engine.

BLAST was introduced in 1990 by [Altschul et al.](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0022-2836(05)80360-2) and has been cited over 100,000 times. Its key insight: **instead of aligning a query against every position in a database, first identify short exact or near-exact matches (seeds), then extend only the promising ones.**

### The BLAST Pipeline

BLAST operates in three stages, each progressively more expensive but applied to fewer candidates:

```
Stage 1: Word matching (very fast, many hits)
    ↓  filter
Stage 2: Ungapped extension (fast, fewer hits)
    ↓  filter
Stage 3: Gapped extension (slow, few hits → final alignments)
```

### Stage 1: The Word Lookup Table

This is where indexing enters the picture. BLAST breaks the **query** sequence into overlapping **words** (short subsequences of length $w$). For protein BLAST (blastp), the default word size is $w = 3$; for nucleotide BLAST (blastn), it is $w = 11$.

For a query protein of length $m$, this produces $m - w + 1$ overlapping words:

```
Query:  M  E  T  H  I  O  N  I  N  E
Words:  MET  ETH  THI  HIO  ION  ONI  NIN  INE
        (w=3, so 10 - 3 + 1 = 8 words)
```

But here is BLAST's clever trick: it doesn't just look for **exact** word matches. For each query word, BLAST generates a **neighborhood** -- all words that score above a threshold $T$ when compared using a substitution matrix (like BLOSUM62, which you saw in the previous lecture).

For example, the word `MET` might have neighbors like `MEA`, `MES`, `LET` -- any 3-mer that scores $\geq T$ against `MET` using BLOSUM62. Lowering $T$ increases sensitivity (more neighbors, more potential matches) but slows the search.

### The Lookup Table

All neighborhood words are organized into a **lookup table** -- essentially a hash table that maps each word to the query positions where it (or one of its neighbors) appears:

| Word | Query position(s) |
|------|-------------------|
| MET | 0 |
| MEA | 0 |
| LET | 0 |
| ETH | 1 |
| ... | ... |

BLAST then scans the database sequence and checks each database word against this lookup table. Because lookup tables provide **O(1)** access (the same hash table concept from Section 4), this scan is extremely fast -- the dominant cost is simply reading the database.

> **Connection to Section 4 (Hashing)**: The BLAST lookup table is a direct application of the hash tables we discussed earlier. Each word is hashed to a bucket, and checking whether a database word has a query match is a constant-time hash lookup. This is what makes BLAST so fast: the expensive Smith-Waterman alignment is never run unless the lookup table produces a hit.

### Stage 2: Ungapped Extension

Each lookup table hit (called a **seed**) is extended in both directions **without gaps**, computing a running alignment score. Extension continues as long as the score stays close to its running maximum. If the score drops by more than a threshold $X$ below the maximum (the **X-drop** criterion), extension stops.

If the resulting ungapped alignment -- called a **High-scoring Segment Pair (HSP)** -- scores above a cutoff, it passes to the next stage. Most seeds are eliminated here.

> **Connection to Lecture 13**: This is exactly the ungapped extension step you saw in the LASTZ pipeline. The X-drop criterion is the same idea.

### Stage 3: Gapped Extension

Surviving HSPs are extended using **gapped** Smith-Waterman alignment (the full dynamic programming algorithm from Lecture 13). This is the most computationally expensive step, but by this point only a tiny fraction of the database remains as candidates.

The final alignments are scored, and statistical significance is assessed using **E-values** (expected number of alignments with this score or better that would occur by chance in a database of this size).

### BLAST vs. Newer Aligners

| Feature | BLAST | Bowtie2 / BWA-MEM |
|---------|-------|-------------------|
| **Primary use** | Query vs. database (homology search) | Reads vs. reference genome (mapping) |
| **Index** | Lookup table from query words | FM index of reference genome |
| **Word size** | 3 (protein), 11 (nucleotide) | 22 (Bowtie2), variable MEMs (BWA-MEM) |
| **Index built on** | Query sequence | Reference genome (built once) |
| **Substitution matrix** | BLOSUM62 (protein), match/mismatch (DNA) | Match/mismatch penalties |
| **Sensitivity** | High (neighborhood words) | Tuned for fast mapping |
| **Speed** | Fast for database search | Faster for read mapping |

The critical difference: BLAST indexes the **query** and scans the **database**, while Bowtie2/BWA-MEM index the **reference** (once) and map **reads** against it. When you have billions of short reads to map against a single reference, pre-indexing the reference is far more efficient.

> **Key Reference**: Altschul SF, Gish W, Miller W, Myers EW, Lipman DJ. "Basic local alignment search tool." *Journal of Molecular Biology* 215, 403-410 (1990). [DOI: 10.1016/S0022-2836(05)80360-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0022-2836(05)80360-2)

## 6. Tries

Now let's move from hash-based lookups to **tree-based** data structures. A **trie** (often pronounced to rhyme with "try" to distinguish it from "tree," though both pronunciations are used -- the name comes from re**trie**val) is a tree-based data structure where:

- Each **edge** is labeled with a single character
- Each **node** represents a prefix of some stored key
- There is at most **one outgoing edge per character** from any node
- Keys are **spelled out** along root-to-leaf paths

### Why Tries?

Tries give us **O(m)** lookup time for a query of length $m$ -- independent of how many keys are stored. This is ideal for searching patterns in indexed text.

> **Why tries matter in biology**: Tries are the foundation for tools like **Kraken** (for taxonomic classification of metagenomic reads), which builds a trie of k-mers labeled with taxonomic IDs to classify millions of reads per minute.

### Using Tries for Substring Indexing

We can build a trie from all substrings of length $L$ extracted from a text $T$:

1. Extract each L-mer and its position
2. Insert each L-mer into the trie, storing position(s) at the leaf
3. To query: walk down the trie following the pattern characters

If at any point there is no edge matching the next character, the pattern does not exist in the index.

```{=html}

<div id="viz-trie" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Interactive Trie Builder</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">Enter a text and substring length to build a trie. Type a pattern in the search field to see the path traced through the trie.</p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:200px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Text:</label>
    <input id="tr-text" type="text" value="ABAB" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <div>
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Substring length:</label>
    <input id="tr-len" type="number" value="2" min="1" max="6" style="width:70px; padding:6px; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="tr-build" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Build Trie</button>
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Search:</label>
    <input id="tr-search" type="text" placeholder="type to search..." style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
</div>
<svg id="tr-svg" width="100%" height="360" style="border:1px solid #eee; border-radius:4px; background:#fafafa;"></svg>
<div id="tr-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; margin-top:8px; min-height:30px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
  let trieRoot = null;
  let nodePositions = [];

  function makeTrie() {
    return {children: {}, positions: [], id: 0};
  }

  function insertTrie(root, word, pos) {
    let node = root;
    for (const ch of word) {
      if (!node.children[ch]) node.children[ch] = makeTrie();
      node = node.children[ch];
    }
    node.positions.push(pos);
  }

  let nextId = 0;
  function assignIds(node) {
    node.id = nextId++;
    for (const ch of Object.keys(node.children).sort()) assignIds(node.children[ch]);
  }

  function layoutTree(node, depth, left, right) {
    const x = (left + right) / 2;
    const y = 40 + depth * 70;
    const result = [{node, x, y, children: []}];
    const kids = Object.keys(node.children).sort();
    if (kids.length > 0) {
      const step = (right - left) / kids.length;
      kids.forEach((ch, i) => {
        const childLayout = layoutTree(node.children[ch], depth + 1, left + i * step, left + (i + 1) * step);
        result[0].children.push({char: ch, layout: childLayout});
        result.push(...childLayout);
      });
    }
    return result;
  }

  function renderTrie(highlight) {
    const svg = $('tr-svg');
    const w = svg.clientWidth || 860;
    if (!trieRoot) { svg.innerHTML = '<text x="' + w/2 + '" y="180" text-anchor="middle" fill="#999">Click "Build Trie" to start</text>'; return; }

    nextId = 0;
    assignIds(trieRoot);
    const layout = layoutTree(trieRoot, 0, 20, w - 20);
    nodePositions = layout;

    const hl = highlight || new Set();
    let html = '';
    // Draw edges
    layout.forEach(item => {
      item.children.forEach(c => {
        const child = c.layout[0];
        const edgeHl = hl.has(item.node.id) && hl.has(child.node.id);
        const color = edgeHl ? '#4CAF50' : '#999';
        const sw = edgeHl ? 3 : 1.5;
        html += `<line x1="${item.x}" y1="${item.y}" x2="${child.x}" y2="${child.y}" stroke="${color}" stroke-width="${sw}"/>`;
        const mx = (item.x + child.x) / 2 - 5;
        const my = (item.y + child.y) / 2;
        html += `<text x="${mx}" y="${my}" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="${edgeHl ? '#2E7D32' : '#2196F3'}">${c.char}</text>`;
      });
    });
    // Draw nodes
    layout.forEach(item => {
      const isLeaf = Object.keys(item.node.children).length === 0;
      const nodeHl = hl.has(item.node.id);
      const fill = nodeHl ? '#4CAF50' : (isLeaf ? '#FF9800' : '#2196F3');
      const r = isLeaf ? 14 : 10;
      html += `<circle cx="${item.x}" cy="${item.y}" r="${r}" fill="${fill}" stroke="white" stroke-width="2" style="cursor:pointer;" data-nid="${item.node.id}"/>`;
      if (isLeaf && item.node.positions.length > 0) {
        html += `<text x="${item.x}" y="${item.y + 4}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="white" font-weight="bold">${item.node.positions.join(',')}</text>`;
      }
    });
    svg.innerHTML = html;
  }

  function buildTrie() {
    const text = $('tr-text').value.toUpperCase();
    const L = parseInt($('tr-len').value);
    trieRoot = makeTrie();
    for (let i = 0; i <= text.length - L; i++) {
      insertTrie(trieRoot, text.substring(i, i + L), i);
    }
    renderTrie();
    $('tr-log').innerHTML = `Trie built from <strong>${text}</strong> with ${L}-mers.`;
  }

  function searchTrie() {
    const query = $('tr-search').value.toUpperCase();
    if (!trieRoot || query.length === 0) { renderTrie(); return; }
    const hl = new Set();
    let node = trieRoot;
    hl.add(node.id);
    let found = true;
    for (const ch of query) {
      if (node.children[ch]) {
        node = node.children[ch];
        hl.add(node.id);
      } else {
        found = false;
        break;
      }
    }
    renderTrie(hl);
    if (found) {
      const posInfo = node.positions.length > 0 ? ` at position(s): ${node.positions.join(', ')}` : ' (prefix match, not a complete indexed substring)';
      $('tr-log').innerHTML = `<span style="color:#4CAF50;"><strong>Found "${query}"</strong>${posInfo}</span>`;
    } else {
      $('tr-log').innerHTML = `<span style="color:#f44336;"><strong>"${query}" not found</strong> -- path ended (no matching edge).</span>`;
    }
  }

  $('tr-build').addEventListener('click', buildTrie);
  $('tr-search').addEventListener('input', searchTrie);
  buildTrie();
})();
</script>
```

### Step-by-Step Trie Construction

Watch how the trie grows as each substring is inserted one at a time. New nodes and edges added at each step are highlighted in green.

```{=html}

<div id="viz-trie-step" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Step-by-Step Trie Construction</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">Step through each substring insertion to see the trie grow incrementally.</p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:200px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Text:</label>
    <input id="trs-text" type="text" value="ABAB" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <div>
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Substring length:</label>
    <input id="trs-len" type="number" value="2" min="1" max="6" style="width:70px; padding:6px; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="trs-reset" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Reset</button>
</div>
<div style="display:flex; gap:8px; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap;">
  <button id="trs-prev" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#78909C; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">&larr; Prev</button>
  <button id="trs-next" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#4CAF50; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Next &rarr;</button>
  <button id="trs-play" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#FF9800; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">&#9654; Play</button>
  <span id="trs-counter" style="font-size:0.9em; color:#666; margin-left:8px;">Step 0 / 0</span>
</div>
<svg id="trs-svg" width="100%" height="360" style="border:1px solid #eee; border-radius:4px; background:#fafafa;"></svg>
<div id="trs-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; margin-top:8px; min-height:30px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
  let substrings = [];
  let step = 0;
  let playTimer = null;

  function makeTrie() { return {children: {}, positions: [], _id: 0}; }
  let gid = 0;

  function insertTrie(root, word, pos) {
    let node = root;
    const newIds = new Set();
    for (const ch of word) {
      if (!node.children[ch]) {
        node.children[ch] = makeTrie();
        node.children[ch]._id = gid++;
        newIds.add(node.children[ch]._id);
      }
      node = node.children[ch];
    }
    node.positions.push(pos);
    return newIds;
  }

  function layoutTree(node, depth, left, right) {
    const x = (left + right) / 2;
    const y = 40 + depth * 70;
    const entry = {node, x, y, childEntries: []};
    const kids = Object.keys(node.children).sort();
    if (kids.length > 0) {
      const step = (right - left) / kids.length;
      kids.forEach((ch, i) => {
        const ce = layoutTree(node.children[ch], depth + 1, left + i * step, left + (i + 1) * step);
        entry.childEntries.push({char: ch, entry: ce});
      });
    }
    return entry;
  }

  function flatL(e) { let a = [e]; e.childEntries.forEach(c => { a = a.concat(flatL(c.entry)); }); return a; }

  function renderTrie(root, newIds) {
    const svg = $('trs-svg');
    const w = svg.clientWidth || 860;
    const layout = layoutTree(root, 0, 20, w - 20);
    const flat = flatL(layout);
    const maxY = Math.max(...flat.map(e => e.y)) + 40;
    svg.setAttribute('height', Math.max(maxY, 200));
    const hl = newIds || new Set();
    let html = '';
    function drawEdges(entry) {
      entry.childEntries.forEach(c => {
        const ce = c.entry;
        const isNew = hl.has(ce.node._id);
        const color = isNew ? '#4CAF50' : '#999';
        const sw = isNew ? 3 : 1.5;
        html += `<line x1="${entry.x}" y1="${entry.y}" x2="${ce.x}" y2="${ce.y}" stroke="${color}" stroke-width="${sw}"/>`;
        const mx = (entry.x + ce.x) / 2 - 5;
        const my = (entry.y + ce.y) / 2;
        html += `<text x="${mx}" y="${my}" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="${isNew ? '#2E7D32' : '#2196F3'}">${c.char}</text>`;
        drawEdges(ce);
      });
    }
    drawEdges(layout);
    flat.forEach(item => {
      const isLeaf = Object.keys(item.node.children).length === 0;
      const isNew = hl.has(item.node._id);
      const fill = isNew ? '#4CAF50' : (isLeaf ? '#FF9800' : '#2196F3');
      const r = isLeaf ? 14 : 10;
      html += `<circle cx="${item.x}" cy="${item.y}" r="${r}" fill="${fill}" stroke="white" stroke-width="2"/>`;
      if (isLeaf && item.node.positions.length > 0) {
        html += `<text x="${item.x}" y="${item.y + 4}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="white" font-weight="bold">${item.node.positions.join(',')}</text>`;
      }
    });
    svg.innerHTML = html;
  }

  function reset() {
    if (playTimer) { clearInterval(playTimer); playTimer = null; $('trs-play').innerHTML = '&#9654; Play'; }
    const text = $('trs-text').value.toUpperCase();
    const L = parseInt($('trs-len').value);
    substrings = [];
    for (let i = 0; i <= text.length - L; i++) {
      substrings.push({word: text.substring(i, i + L), pos: i});
    }
    step = 0;
    gid = 1;
    renderStep();
  }

  function renderStep() {
    gid = 1;
    const root = makeTrie(); root._id = 0;
    let lastNewIds = new Set();
    for (let i = 0; i < step; i++) {
      const ids = insertTrie(root, substrings[i].word, substrings[i].pos);
      if (i === step - 1) lastNewIds = ids;
    }
    renderTrie(root, lastNewIds);
    $('trs-counter').textContent = `Step ${step} / ${substrings.length}`;
    if (step === 0) {
      $('trs-log').innerHTML = 'Click <strong>Next</strong> or <strong>Play</strong> to begin inserting substrings.';
    } else {
      const s = substrings[step - 1];
      const newCount = lastNewIds.size;
      $('trs-log').innerHTML = `Step ${step}: Inserted "<strong>${s.word}</strong>" (position ${s.pos}).` +
        (newCount > 0 ? ` <span style="color:#4CAF50;">Added ${newCount} new node(s).</span>` : ' <span style="color:#2196F3;">No new nodes needed (path already existed).</span>');
    }
  }

  function nextStep() {
    if (step < substrings.length) { step++; renderStep(); }
    else if (playTimer) { clearInterval(playTimer); playTimer = null; $('trs-play').innerHTML = '&#9654; Play'; }
  }

  function prevStep() {
    if (step > 0) { step--; renderStep(); }
  }

  function togglePlay() {
    if (playTimer) {
      clearInterval(playTimer); playTimer = null;
      $('trs-play').innerHTML = '&#9654; Play';
    } else {
      if (step >= substrings.length) { step = 0; renderStep(); }
      $('trs-play').innerHTML = '&#9724; Pause';
      playTimer = setInterval(() => { nextStep(); }, 800);
    }
  }

  $('trs-reset').addEventListener('click', reset);
  $('trs-prev').addEventListener('click', prevStep);
  $('trs-next').addEventListener('click', nextStep);
  $('trs-play').addEventListener('click', togglePlay);
  reset();
})();
</script>
```

## 7. Suffix Tries

The substring index approach requires choosing a fixed length $L$. But what if we want to find **any** substring, of **any** length? The answer is to index **all suffixes** of the text. This is directly relevant to genomics: when aligning a read, we don't know in advance how long the matching region will be (due to mutations, indels, and varying read lengths), so we need an index that can handle queries of any length.

### What is a Suffix?

A suffix of a string $T$ is any substring that extends to the end. For $T = $ `abaaba`:

| Index | Suffix |
|-------|--------|
| 0 | abaaba |
| 1 | baaba |
| 2 | aaba |
| 3 | aba |
| 4 | ba |
| 5 | a |

### The Sentinel Character

We append a special character `$` to the end of the text. The `$` is **lexicographically smaller** than any other character and appears nowhere else. This ensures:

1. No suffix is a prefix of another suffix
2. Every suffix ends at a unique leaf in the trie

So $T = $ `abaaba$` has suffixes: `abaaba$`, `baaba$`, `aaba$`, `aba$`, `ba$`, `a$`, `$`.

### Building a Suffix Trie

A **suffix trie** is simply a trie built from all suffixes of $T$. Insert each suffix one by one.

### Operations on a Suffix Trie

Given a suffix trie of text $T$ and a query pattern $P$:

1. **Is $P$ a substring of $T$?** Follow the path for $P$. If you can follow all characters, yes.
2. **Is $P$ a suffix of $T$?** Follow the path for $P$. The path must end at a node with a `$` edge leading to a leaf.
3. **How many times does $P$ occur?** Follow the path for $P$, then count the number of leaves in the subtree below.
4. **What is the longest repeated substring?** Find the deepest internal node (node with multiple children that is not a leaf).

### Worked Example: `abaaba$`

Let's trace through searching for `aba` in the suffix trie of `abaaba$`:

- Start at root
- Follow edge `a` -- found, continue
- Follow edge `b` -- found, continue
- Follow edge `a` -- found, arrived at a node

Since we followed all characters successfully, `aba` **is a substring**. The subtree below has 2 leaves (positions 0 and 3), so `aba` occurs **2 times**.

Now search for `abc`:

- Follow edge `a` -- found
- Follow edge `b` -- found
- Follow edge `c` -- **no such edge!** Fall off the trie. `abc` is **not a substring**.

```{=html}

<div id="viz-suffix-trie" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Interactive Suffix Trie</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">Enter a short string to build its suffix trie. Search for patterns to see the path traced (green = match, red = fall-off).</p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Text (keep to 5-6 chars -- suffix tries grow quadratically!):</label>
    <input id="st-text" type="text" value="abaaba" maxlength="8" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="st-build" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Build Suffix Trie</button>
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Search pattern:</label>
    <input id="st-search" type="text" placeholder="e.g. aba" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
</div>
<svg id="st-svg" width="100%" height="450" style="border:1px solid #eee; border-radius:4px; background:#fafafa; overflow:visible;"></svg>
<div id="st-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; margin-top:8px; min-height:30px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);

  function makeNode() { return {children: {}, suffixIndex: -1, _id: 0}; }
  let gid = 0;

  function buildSuffixTrie(text) {
    gid = 0;
    const root = makeNode();
    root._id = gid++;
    for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
      let node = root;
      for (let j = i; j < text.length; j++) {
        const ch = text[j];
        if (!node.children[ch]) {
          node.children[ch] = makeNode();
          node.children[ch]._id = gid++;
        }
        node = node.children[ch];
      }
      node.suffixIndex = i;
    }
    return root;
  }

  function countLeaves(node) {
    const kids = Object.keys(node.children);
    if (kids.length === 0) return 1;
    let c = 0;
    kids.forEach(k => c += countLeaves(node.children[k]));
    return c;
  }

  function layoutST(node, depth, left, right) {
    const x = (left + right) / 2;
    const y = 30 + depth * 55;
    const entry = {node, x, y, childEntries: []};
    const kids = Object.keys(node.children).sort();
    if (kids.length > 0) {
      const step = (right - left) / kids.length;
      kids.forEach((ch, i) => {
        const childEntry = layoutST(node.children[ch], depth + 1, left + i * step, left + (i + 1) * step);
        entry.childEntries.push({char: ch, entry: childEntry});
      });
    }
    return entry;
  }

  function flattenLayout(entry) {
    let arr = [entry];
    entry.childEntries.forEach(c => { arr = arr.concat(flattenLayout(c.entry)); });
    return arr;
  }

  function renderST(root, highlightIds, failId) {
    const svg = $('st-svg');
    const w = svg.clientWidth || 860;
    const layout = layoutST(root, 0, 10, w - 10);
    const flat = flattenLayout(layout);
    const maxY = Math.max(...flat.map(e => e.y)) + 40;
    svg.setAttribute('height', Math.max(maxY, 200));

    const hl = highlightIds || new Set();
    let html = '';

    function drawEdges(entry) {
      entry.childEntries.forEach(c => {
        const ce = c.entry;
        const bothHl = hl.has(entry.node._id) && hl.has(ce.node._id);
        const isFail = failId !== undefined && ((entry.node._id === failId) || (ce.node._id === failId));
        const color = isFail && bothHl ? '#f44336' : bothHl ? '#4CAF50' : '#bbb';
        const sw = bothHl ? 2.5 : 1;
        html += `<line x1="${entry.x}" y1="${entry.y}" x2="${ce.x}" y2="${ce.y}" stroke="${color}" stroke-width="${sw}"/>`;
        const mx = (entry.x + ce.x) / 2;
        const my = (entry.y + ce.y) / 2 - 4;
        html += `<text x="${mx}" y="${my}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="${bothHl ? color : '#2196F3'}">${c.char}</text>`;
        drawEdges(ce);
      });
    }
    drawEdges(layout);

    flat.forEach(e => {
      const isLeaf = Object.keys(e.node.children).length === 0;
      const inPath = hl.has(e.node._id);
      const fill = inPath ? '#4CAF50' : (isLeaf ? '#FF9800' : '#ccc');
      const r = isLeaf ? 12 : 7;
      html += `<circle cx="${e.x}" cy="${e.y}" r="${r}" fill="${fill}" stroke="white" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
      if (isLeaf && e.node.suffixIndex >= 0) {
        html += `<text x="${e.x}" y="${e.y + 4}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="white" font-weight="bold">${e.node.suffixIndex}</text>`;
      }
    });
    svg.innerHTML = html;
  }

  let currentRoot = null;

  function build() {
    const text = $('st-text').value.toLowerCase() + '$';
    currentRoot = buildSuffixTrie(text);
    renderST(currentRoot);
    $('st-log').innerHTML = `Suffix trie built for "<strong>${text}</strong>" (${text.length} suffixes). Leaf numbers = suffix starting positions.`;
  }

  function search() {
    const pattern = $('st-search').value.toLowerCase();
    if (!currentRoot || pattern.length === 0) { if (currentRoot) renderST(currentRoot); return; }
    const hl = new Set();
    let node = currentRoot;
    hl.add(node._id);
    let failNode;
    let found = true;
    for (const ch of pattern) {
      if (node.children[ch]) {
        node = node.children[ch];
        hl.add(node._id);
      } else {
        found = false;
        failNode = node._id;
        break;
      }
    }
    renderST(currentRoot, hl, failNode);
    if (found) {
      const occ = countLeaves(node);
      const isSuffix = node.children['$'] !== undefined || Object.keys(node.children).length === 0;
      let msg = `<span style="color:#4CAF50;"><strong>"${pattern}" found!</strong> Occurs <strong>${occ}</strong> time(s).`;
      if (isSuffix) msg += ` It is also a suffix.`;
      msg += `</span>`;
      $('st-log').innerHTML = msg;
    } else {
      $('st-log').innerHTML = `<span style="color:#f44336;"><strong>"${pattern}" NOT found.</strong> No edge for the next character -- fell off the trie.</span>`;
    }
  }

  $('st-build').addEventListener('click', build);
  $('st-search').addEventListener('input', search);
  build();
})();
</script>
```

### Step-by-Step Suffix Trie Construction

Watch each suffix being inserted one at a time. The newest suffix's path is highlighted in green so you can see how the trie grows with each insertion.

```{=html}

<div id="viz-st-step" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Step-by-Step Suffix Trie Construction</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">Each step inserts one suffix. Green highlights show nodes added or traversed for the latest suffix.</p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Text (keep short!):</label>
    <input id="sts-text" type="text" value="abab" maxlength="7" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="sts-reset" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Reset</button>
</div>
<div style="display:flex; gap:8px; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap;">
  <button id="sts-prev" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#78909C; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">&larr; Prev</button>
  <button id="sts-next" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#4CAF50; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Next &rarr;</button>
  <button id="sts-play" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#FF9800; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">&#9654; Play</button>
  <span id="sts-counter" style="font-size:0.9em; color:#666; margin-left:8px;">Step 0 / 0</span>
</div>
<svg id="sts-svg" width="100%" height="450" style="border:1px solid #eee; border-radius:4px; background:#fafafa; overflow:visible;"></svg>
<div id="sts-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; margin-top:8px; min-height:30px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
  let fullText = '';
  let suffixes = [];
  let step = 0;
  let playTimer = null;

  function makeNode() { return {children: {}, suffIdx: -1, _id: 0}; }
  let gid = 0;

  function insertSuffix(root, text, startIdx) {
    let node = root;
    const touchedIds = new Set();
    touchedIds.add(node._id);
    const newIds = new Set();
    for (let j = startIdx; j < text.length; j++) {
      const ch = text[j];
      if (!node.children[ch]) {
        node.children[ch] = makeNode();
        node.children[ch]._id = gid++;
        newIds.add(node.children[ch]._id);
      }
      node = node.children[ch];
      touchedIds.add(node._id);
    }
    node.suffIdx = startIdx;
    return {touchedIds, newIds};
  }

  function layoutST(node, depth, left, right) {
    const x = (left + right) / 2;
    const y = 30 + depth * 55;
    const entry = {node, x, y, childEntries: []};
    const kids = Object.keys(node.children).sort();
    if (kids.length > 0) {
      const s = (right - left) / kids.length;
      kids.forEach((ch, i) => {
        const ce = layoutST(node.children[ch], depth + 1, left + i * s, left + (i + 1) * s);
        entry.childEntries.push({char: ch, entry: ce});
      });
    }
    return entry;
  }

  function flatL(e) { let a = [e]; e.childEntries.forEach(c => { a = a.concat(flatL(c.entry)); }); return a; }

  function renderST(root, touchedIds, newIds) {
    const svg = $('sts-svg');
    const w = svg.clientWidth || 860;
    const layout = layoutST(root, 0, 10, w - 10);
    const flat = flatL(layout);
    const maxY = Math.max(...flat.map(e => e.y)) + 40;
    svg.setAttribute('height', Math.max(maxY, 200));
    const touched = touchedIds || new Set();
    const added = newIds || new Set();
    let html = '';
    function drawEdges(entry) {
      entry.childEntries.forEach(c => {
        const ce = c.entry;
        const isNew = added.has(ce.node._id);
        const isTouched = touched.has(entry.node._id) && touched.has(ce.node._id);
        const color = isNew ? '#4CAF50' : isTouched ? '#81C784' : '#bbb';
        const sw = isTouched ? 2.5 : 1;
        html += `<line x1="${entry.x}" y1="${entry.y}" x2="${ce.x}" y2="${ce.y}" stroke="${color}" stroke-width="${sw}"/>`;
        const mx = (entry.x + ce.x) / 2;
        const my = (entry.y + ce.y) / 2 - 4;
        html += `<text x="${mx}" y="${my}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="${isTouched ? '#2E7D32' : '#2196F3'}">${c.char}</text>`;
        drawEdges(ce);
      });
    }
    drawEdges(layout);
    flat.forEach(e => {
      const isLeaf = Object.keys(e.node.children).length === 0;
      const isNew = added.has(e.node._id);
      const isTouched = touched.has(e.node._id);
      const fill = isNew ? '#4CAF50' : isTouched ? '#81C784' : (isLeaf ? '#FF9800' : '#ccc');
      const r = isLeaf ? 12 : 7;
      html += `<circle cx="${e.x}" cy="${e.y}" r="${r}" fill="${fill}" stroke="white" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
      if (isLeaf && e.node.suffIdx >= 0) {
        html += `<text x="${e.x}" y="${e.y + 4}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="white" font-weight="bold">${e.node.suffIdx}</text>`;
      }
    });
    svg.innerHTML = html;
  }

  function reset() {
    if (playTimer) { clearInterval(playTimer); playTimer = null; $('sts-play').innerHTML = '&#9654; Play'; }
    fullText = $('sts-text').value.toLowerCase() + '$';
    suffixes = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < fullText.length; i++) {
      suffixes.push({start: i, text: fullText.substring(i)});
    }
    step = 0;
    renderStep();
  }

  function renderStep() {
    gid = 1;
    const root = makeNode(); root._id = 0;
    let lastTouched = new Set();
    let lastNew = new Set();
    for (let i = 0; i < step; i++) {
      const result = insertSuffix(root, fullText, suffixes[i].start);
      if (i === step - 1) {
        lastTouched = result.touchedIds;
        lastNew = result.newIds;
      }
    }
    renderST(root, lastTouched, lastNew);
    $('sts-counter').textContent = `Step ${step} / ${suffixes.length}`;
    if (step === 0) {
      $('sts-log').innerHTML = `Text: "<strong>${fullText}</strong>" (${suffixes.length} suffixes). Click <strong>Next</strong> or <strong>Play</strong> to insert suffixes one by one.`;
    } else {
      const s = suffixes[step - 1];
      $('sts-log').innerHTML = `Step ${step}: Inserted suffix "<strong>${s.text}</strong>" (starting at position ${s.start}).` +
        (lastNew.size > 0 ? ` <span style="color:#4CAF50;">Added ${lastNew.size} new node(s).</span>` : ' <span style="color:#2196F3;">No new nodes needed.</span>');
    }
  }

  function nextStep() {
    if (step < suffixes.length) { step++; renderStep(); }
    else if (playTimer) { clearInterval(playTimer); playTimer = null; $('sts-play').innerHTML = '&#9654; Play'; }
  }
  function prevStep() { if (step > 0) { step--; renderStep(); } }
  function togglePlay() {
    if (playTimer) {
      clearInterval(playTimer); playTimer = null;
      $('sts-play').innerHTML = '&#9654; Play';
    } else {
      if (step >= suffixes.length) { step = 0; renderStep(); }
      $('sts-play').innerHTML = '&#9724; Pause';
      playTimer = setInterval(() => { nextStep(); }, 1000);
    }
  }

  $('sts-reset').addEventListener('click', reset);
  $('sts-prev').addEventListener('click', prevStep);
  $('sts-next').addEventListener('click', nextStep);
  $('sts-play').addEventListener('click', togglePlay);
  reset();
})();
</script>
```
