## 8. From Tries to Trees (Suffix Trees)

### The Problem with Suffix Tries

Suffix tries are conceptually clean, but they have a major practical problem: **size**. A suffix trie for a text of length $n$ can have up to $O(n^2)$ nodes. For a genome of 3 billion base pairs, that is simply too much.

### The Solution: Collapse Non-Branching Paths

A **suffix tree** is obtained by taking a suffix trie and **collapsing** every path of non-branching nodes into a single edge. Instead of one character per edge, each edge is labeled with a *substring*.

For example, in a suffix trie if you have a chain: root --a--> node1 --b--> node2 --a--> leaf, and node1 and node2 each have only one child, we collapse this to: root --aba--> leaf.

### Properties of Suffix Trees

| Property | Suffix Trie | Suffix Tree |
|----------|-------------|-------------|
| Nodes | $O(n^2)$ | $O(n)$ |
| Edges | $O(n^2)$ | $O(n)$ |
| Edge labels | Single characters | Substrings |
| Build time | $O(n^2)$ | $O(n)$ (Ukkonen's algorithm) |

The suffix tree has **at most $2n$ nodes** (for a text of length $n$), making it linear in size.

### Same Operations, More Compact

All the operations we could do with a suffix trie work on suffix trees too:

- Check if a pattern exists: follow edges, potentially matching partway through an edge
- Count occurrences: count leaves below the match point
- Find longest repeated substring: deepest internal node (counting total characters on path)

### Suffix Trees in Practice: MUMmer

The [MUMmer](http://mummer.sourceforge.net/) tool uses suffix trees to rapidly align whole genomes against each other. It finds **Maximal Unique Matches (MUMs)** -- long stretches that occur exactly once in each genome -- as anchors for whole-genome alignment. MUMmer was used to compare the first assembled human genomes and remains the go-to tool for bacterial genome comparisons, capable of aligning two 5 Mb bacterial genomes in seconds.

### Step-by-Step: From Suffix Trie to Suffix Tree

Watch the suffix trie being built suffix by suffix, then see it collapse into a suffix tree. This shows both the quadratic growth of the trie and the dramatic compression when non-branching paths are merged.

```{=html}

<div id="viz-collapse-step" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Step-by-Step: Build Suffix Trie, Then Collapse to Tree</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">First build the suffix trie step by step, then click "Collapse to Tree" to watch non-branching paths merge.</p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Text:</label>
    <input id="cs-text" type="text" value="abab" maxlength="7" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="cs-reset" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Reset</button>
</div>
<div style="display:flex; gap:8px; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap;">
  <button id="cs-prev" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#78909C; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">&larr; Prev</button>
  <button id="cs-next" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#4CAF50; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Next &rarr;</button>
  <button id="cs-play" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#FF9800; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">&#9654; Play</button>
  <button id="cs-collapse" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#9C27B0; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Collapse to Tree</button>
  <span id="cs-counter" style="font-size:0.9em; color:#666; margin-left:8px;">Step 0 / 0</span>
</div>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:400px;">
    <div id="cs-left-label" style="text-align:center; font-weight:bold; color:#666; margin-bottom:4px;">Suffix Trie (building...)</div>
    <svg id="cs-trie-svg" width="100%" height="400" style="border:1px solid #eee; border-radius:4px; background:#fafafa; overflow:visible;"></svg>
  </div>
  <div id="cs-right-panel" style="flex:1; min-width:400px; display:none;">
    <div style="text-align:center; font-weight:bold; color:#9C27B0; margin-bottom:4px;">Suffix Tree (collapsed)</div>
    <svg id="cs-tree-svg" width="100%" height="400" style="border:1px solid #f3e5f5; border-radius:4px; background:#fdf5ff; overflow:visible;"></svg>
  </div>
</div>
<div id="cs-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; margin-top:8px; min-height:30px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
  let fullText = '';
  let suffixes = [];
  let step = 0;
  let playTimer = null;
  let collapsed = false;

  function makeNode() { return {children: {}, suffIdx: -1, _id: 0}; }
  let gid = 0;

  function insertSuffix(root, text, startIdx) {
    let node = root;
    for (let j = startIdx; j < text.length; j++) {
      const ch = text[j];
      if (!node.children[ch]) {
        node.children[ch] = makeNode();
        node.children[ch]._id = gid++;
      }
      node = node.children[ch];
    }
    node.suffIdx = startIdx;
  }

  function collapseToTree(trieNode) {
    const treeNode = {children: {}, suffIdx: trieNode.suffIdx, _id: gid++, label: ''};
    const keys = Object.keys(trieNode.children).sort();
    keys.forEach(ch => {
      let label = ch;
      let child = trieNode.children[ch];
      while (Object.keys(child.children).length === 1 && child.suffIdx < 0) {
        const nextCh = Object.keys(child.children)[0];
        label += nextCh;
        child = child.children[nextCh];
      }
      const coll = collapseToTree(child);
      coll.label = label;
      treeNode.children[label] = coll;
    });
    return treeNode;
  }

  function layoutGeneric(node, getKids, depth, left, right) {
    const x = (left + right) / 2;
    const y = 30 + depth * 60;
    const entry = {node, x, y, childEntries: []};
    const kids = getKids(node);
    if (kids.length > 0) {
      const s = (right - left) / kids.length;
      kids.forEach((k, i) => {
        const ce = layoutGeneric(k.child, getKids, depth + 1, left + i * s, left + (i + 1) * s);
        entry.childEntries.push({label: k.label, entry: ce});
      });
    }
    return entry;
  }

  function flatL(e) { let a = [e]; e.childEntries.forEach(c => { a = a.concat(flatL(c.entry)); }); return a; }

  function renderGeneric(svgEl, layout, highlightColor) {
    const flat = flatL(layout);
    const maxY = Math.max(...flat.map(e => e.y)) + 40;
    svgEl.setAttribute('height', Math.max(maxY, 200));
    const edgeColor = highlightColor || '#bbb';
    const labelColor = highlightColor || '#2196F3';
    let html = '';
    function drawEdges(entry) {
      entry.childEntries.forEach(c => {
        const ce = c.entry;
        html += `<line x1="${entry.x}" y1="${entry.y}" x2="${ce.x}" y2="${ce.y}" stroke="${edgeColor}" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
        const mx = (entry.x + ce.x) / 2;
        const my = (entry.y + ce.y) / 2 - 4;
        html += `<text x="${mx}" y="${my}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="${labelColor}">${c.label}</text>`;
        drawEdges(ce);
      });
    }
    drawEdges(layout);
    flat.forEach(e => {
      const isLeaf = e.childEntries.length === 0;
      const fill = isLeaf ? '#FF9800' : '#ccc';
      const r = isLeaf ? 12 : 7;
      html += `<circle cx="${e.x}" cy="${e.y}" r="${r}" fill="${fill}" stroke="white" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
      if (isLeaf && e.node.suffIdx >= 0) {
        html += `<text x="${e.x}" y="${e.y + 4}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="white" font-weight="bold">${e.node.suffIdx}</text>`;
      }
    });
    svgEl.innerHTML = html;
  }

  function getTrieKids(node) {
    return Object.keys(node.children).sort().map(ch => ({label: ch, child: node.children[ch]}));
  }
  function getTreeKids(node) {
    return Object.keys(node.children).sort().map(lbl => ({label: lbl, child: node.children[lbl]}));
  }

  function countNodes(node, getKids) {
    let c = 1;
    getKids(node).forEach(k => { c += countNodes(k.child, getKids); });
    return c;
  }

  function reset() {
    if (playTimer) { clearInterval(playTimer); playTimer = null; $('cs-play').innerHTML = '&#9654; Play'; }
    fullText = $('cs-text').value.toLowerCase() + '$';
    suffixes = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < fullText.length; i++) {
      suffixes.push({start: i, text: fullText.substring(i)});
    }
    step = 0;
    collapsed = false;
    $('cs-right-panel').style.display = 'none';
    $('cs-left-label').textContent = 'Suffix Trie (building...)';
    renderStep();
  }

  function buildTrieUpToStep() {
    gid = 1;
    const root = makeNode(); root._id = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < step; i++) {
      insertSuffix(root, fullText, suffixes[i].start);
    }
    return root;
  }

  function renderStep() {
    const root = buildTrieUpToStep();
    const svg1 = $('cs-trie-svg');
    const w1 = svg1.clientWidth || 420;
    const layout = layoutGeneric(root, getTrieKids, 0, 10, w1 - 10);
    renderGeneric(svg1, layout);
    const nodeCount = countNodes(root, getTrieKids);
    $('cs-counter').textContent = `Step ${step} / ${suffixes.length}`;
    if (step === 0) {
      $('cs-log').innerHTML = `Text: "<strong>${fullText}</strong>" (${suffixes.length} suffixes). Click <strong>Next</strong> to insert suffixes, or <strong>Play</strong> to animate.`;
    } else {
      const s = suffixes[step - 1];
      $('cs-log').innerHTML = `Step ${step}: Inserted suffix "<strong>${s.text}</strong>" (pos ${s.start}). Trie now has <strong>${nodeCount}</strong> nodes.`;
    }
    if (collapsed) doCollapse();
  }

  function doCollapse() {
    collapsed = true;
    const root = buildTrieUpToStep();
    const treeRoot = collapseToTree(root);
    const svg2 = $('cs-tree-svg');
    const w2 = svg2.clientWidth || 420;
    const treeLayout = layoutGeneric(treeRoot, getTreeKids, 0, 10, w2 - 10);
    renderGeneric(svg2, treeLayout, '#9C27B0');
    $('cs-right-panel').style.display = 'block';
    $('cs-left-label').textContent = 'Suffix Trie';
    const trieNodes = countNodes(root, getTrieKids);
    const treeNodes = countNodes(treeRoot, getTreeKids);
    $('cs-log').innerHTML = `Suffix trie: <strong>${trieNodes}</strong> nodes &rarr; Suffix tree: <strong>${treeNodes}</strong> nodes (<strong>${Math.round((1 - treeNodes/trieNodes)*100)}% reduction</strong>). Non-branching paths have been collapsed into multi-character edges.`;
  }

  function nextStep() {
    if (step < suffixes.length) { step++; renderStep(); }
    else if (playTimer) { clearInterval(playTimer); playTimer = null; $('cs-play').innerHTML = '&#9654; Play'; }
  }
  function prevStep() { if (step > 0) { step--; renderStep(); } }
  function togglePlay() {
    if (playTimer) {
      clearInterval(playTimer); playTimer = null;
      $('cs-play').innerHTML = '&#9654; Play';
    } else {
      if (step >= suffixes.length) { step = 0; collapsed = false; $('cs-right-panel').style.display = 'none'; renderStep(); }
      $('cs-play').innerHTML = '&#9724; Pause';
      playTimer = setInterval(() => { nextStep(); }, 1000);
    }
  }

  $('cs-reset').addEventListener('click', reset);
  $('cs-prev').addEventListener('click', prevStep);
  $('cs-next').addEventListener('click', nextStep);
  $('cs-play').addEventListener('click', togglePlay);
  $('cs-collapse').addEventListener('click', doCollapse);
  reset();
})();
</script>
```

### Memory Limitation

Despite having $O(n)$ nodes, suffix trees have large constant factors. Each node stores pointers, edge labels, and suffix links. In practice, a suffix tree for the human genome requires approximately **47 GB of RAM** -- feasible on a server, but not ideal.

```{=html}

<div id="viz-suffix-tree" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Suffix Trie to Suffix Tree Comparison</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">See a suffix trie and its collapsed suffix tree side by side. Search for patterns in the tree.</p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Text:</label>
    <input id="stt-text" type="text" value="abaab" maxlength="7" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="stt-build" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Build Both</button>
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Search pattern:</label>
    <input id="stt-search" type="text" placeholder="e.g. ab" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
</div>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:400px;">
    <div style="text-align:center; font-weight:bold; color:#666; margin-bottom:4px;">Suffix Trie (O(n<sup>2</sup>) nodes)</div>
    <svg id="stt-trie-svg" width="100%" height="350" style="border:1px solid #eee; border-radius:4px; background:#fafafa;"></svg>
  </div>
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:400px;">
    <div style="text-align:center; font-weight:bold; color:#666; margin-bottom:4px;">Suffix Tree (O(n) nodes)</div>
    <svg id="stt-tree-svg" width="100%" height="350" style="border:1px solid #eee; border-radius:4px; background:#fafafa;"></svg>
  </div>
</div>
<div id="stt-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; margin-top:8px; min-height:30px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
  let trieRoot = null, treeRoot = null, fullText = '';

  function makeN() { return {children: {}, suffIdx: -1, _id: 0}; }
  let gid = 0;

  function buildSTrie(text) {
    gid = 0;
    const root = makeN(); root._id = gid++;
    for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
      let nd = root;
      for (let j = i; j < text.length; j++) {
        if (!nd.children[text[j]]) { nd.children[text[j]] = makeN(); nd.children[text[j]]._id = gid++; }
        nd = nd.children[text[j]];
      }
      nd.suffIdx = i;
    }
    return root;
  }

  // Collapse trie into tree
  function collapseToTree(trieNode) {
    const treeNode = {children: {}, suffIdx: trieNode.suffIdx, _id: gid++, label: ''};
    const keys = Object.keys(trieNode.children).sort();
    keys.forEach(ch => {
      let label = ch;
      let child = trieNode.children[ch];
      while (Object.keys(child.children).length === 1 && child.suffIdx < 0) {
        const nextCh = Object.keys(child.children)[0];
        label += nextCh;
        child = child.children[nextCh];
      }
      const collapsed = collapseToTree(child);
      collapsed.label = label;
      treeNode.children[label] = collapsed;
    });
    return treeNode;
  }

  function layoutGeneric(node, getKids, depth, left, right) {
    const x = (left + right) / 2;
    const y = 30 + depth * 65;
    const entry = {node, x, y, childEntries: []};
    const kids = getKids(node);
    if (kids.length > 0) {
      const step = (right - left) / kids.length;
      kids.forEach((k, i) => {
        const ce = layoutGeneric(k.child, getKids, depth + 1, left + i * step, left + (i + 1) * step);
        entry.childEntries.push({label: k.label, entry: ce});
      });
    }
    return entry;
  }

  function flatL(e) { let a = [e]; e.childEntries.forEach(c => { a = a.concat(flatL(c.entry)); }); return a; }

  function renderGeneric(svgEl, layout, hl) {
    const w = svgEl.clientWidth || 420;
    const flat = flatL(layout);
    const maxY = Math.max(...flat.map(e => e.y)) + 30;
    svgEl.setAttribute('height', Math.max(maxY, 200));
    const hlSet = hl || new Set();
    let html = '';
    function drawE(entry) {
      entry.childEntries.forEach(c => {
        const ce = c.entry;
        const both = hlSet.has(entry.node._id) && hlSet.has(ce.node._id);
        const col = both ? '#4CAF50' : '#bbb';
        html += `<line x1="${entry.x}" y1="${entry.y}" x2="${ce.x}" y2="${ce.y}" stroke="${col}" stroke-width="${both?2.5:1}"/>`;
        const mx = (entry.x + ce.x) / 2;
        const my = (entry.y + ce.y) / 2 - 4;
        html += `<text x="${mx}" y="${my}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="${both?'#2E7D32':'#2196F3'}">${c.label}</text>`;
        drawE(ce);
      });
    }
    drawE(layout);
    flat.forEach(e => {
      const isLeaf = e.childEntries.length === 0;
      const inP = hlSet.has(e.node._id);
      const fill = inP ? '#4CAF50' : (isLeaf ? '#FF9800' : '#ccc');
      const r = isLeaf ? 12 : 7;
      html += `<circle cx="${e.x}" cy="${e.y}" r="${r}" fill="${fill}" stroke="white" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
      if (isLeaf && e.node.suffIdx >= 0) {
        html += `<text x="${e.x}" y="${e.y+4}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="white" font-weight="bold">${e.node.suffIdx}</text>`;
      }
    });
    svgEl.innerHTML = html;
  }

  function getTrieKids(node) {
    return Object.keys(node.children).sort().map(ch => ({label: ch, child: node.children[ch]}));
  }
  function getTreeKids(node) {
    return Object.keys(node.children).sort().map(lbl => ({label: lbl, child: node.children[lbl]}));
  }

  function build() {
    fullText = $('stt-text').value.toLowerCase() + '$';
    trieRoot = buildSTrie(fullText);
    treeRoot = collapseToTree(trieRoot);
    const svg1 = $('stt-trie-svg'), svg2 = $('stt-tree-svg');
    const w1 = svg1.clientWidth || 420, w2 = svg2.clientWidth || 420;
    const tLayout = layoutGeneric(trieRoot, getTrieKids, 0, 10, w1 - 10);
    const sLayout = layoutGeneric(treeRoot, getTreeKids, 0, 10, w2 - 10);
    renderGeneric(svg1, tLayout);
    renderGeneric(svg2, sLayout);
    const trieNodes = flatL(tLayout).length;
    const treeNodes = flatL(sLayout).length;
    $('stt-log').innerHTML = `Suffix trie: <strong>${trieNodes}</strong> nodes | Suffix tree: <strong>${treeNodes}</strong> nodes (${Math.round((1-treeNodes/trieNodes)*100)}% reduction).`;
  }

  function search() {
    const pattern = $('stt-search').value.toLowerCase();
    if (!treeRoot || !trieRoot) return;
    const svg1 = $('stt-trie-svg'), svg2 = $('stt-tree-svg');
    const w1 = svg1.clientWidth || 420, w2 = svg2.clientWidth || 420;

    // Search trie
    const hlTrie = new Set();
    let nd = trieRoot; hlTrie.add(nd._id);
    for (const ch of pattern) {
      if (nd.children[ch]) { nd = nd.children[ch]; hlTrie.add(nd._id); } else break;
    }
    const tLayout = layoutGeneric(trieRoot, getTrieKids, 0, 10, w1 - 10);
    renderGeneric(svg1, tLayout, hlTrie);

    // Search tree
    const hlTree = new Set();
    nd = treeRoot; hlTree.add(nd._id);
    let pi = 0; let found = true;
    while (pi < pattern.length) {
      const keys = Object.keys(nd.children).sort();
      let matched = false;
      for (const lbl of keys) {
        if (lbl[0] === pattern[pi]) {
          const child = nd.children[lbl];
          let li = 0;
          while (li < lbl.length && pi < pattern.length && lbl[li] === pattern[pi]) { li++; pi++; }
          hlTree.add(child._id);
          nd = child;
          matched = true;
          break;
        }
      }
      if (!matched) { found = false; break; }
    }
    const sLayout = layoutGeneric(treeRoot, getTreeKids, 0, 10, w2 - 10);
    renderGeneric(svg2, sLayout, hlTree);

    if (found && pattern.length > 0) {
      $('stt-log').innerHTML = `<span style="color:#4CAF50;"><strong>"${pattern}" found</strong> in both structures.</span>`;
    } else if (pattern.length > 0) {
      $('stt-log').innerHTML = `<span style="color:#f44336;"><strong>"${pattern}" not found.</strong></span>`;
    }
  }

  $('stt-build').addEventListener('click', build);
  $('stt-search').addEventListener('input', search);
  build();
})();
</script>
```

---

## 9. Suffix Arrays

### An Even More Compact Representation

Suffix trees solve the node-count problem, but they still carry a lot of overhead: pointers, edge labels, suffix links. Can we do better?

The trade-off we will accept: suffix arrays give up the $O(m)$ query time of suffix trees, settling for $O(m \log n)$ with binary search. But the memory savings -- from ~47 GB down to ~12 GB for the human genome -- make this trade-off worthwhile in practice.

> **Biological application**: Suffix arrays are used internally by many alignment tools and are the basis for the enhanced suffix array used by **STAR** (the most popular RNA-seq aligner).

A **suffix array** is a beautifully simple data structure: it is just an array of integers representing the **sorted order of all suffixes**.

### Construction

Given text $T$ with sentinel `$`:

1. List all suffixes with their starting positions
2. Sort the suffixes **lexicographically**
3. Store only the **starting positions** in sorted order

For $T = $ `abaaba$`:

| Rank | Starting Position | Suffix |
|------|-------------------|--------|
| 0 | 6 | `$` |
| 1 | 5 | `a$` |
| 2 | 2 | `aaba$` |
| 3 | 3 | `aba$` |
| 4 | 0 | `abaaba$` |
| 5 | 4 | `ba$` |
| 6 | 1 | `baaba$` |

The suffix array is: **[6, 5, 2, 3, 0, 4, 1]**

### Searching with Binary Search

Since the suffixes are sorted, we can use **binary search** to find any pattern in $O(m \log n)$ time, where $m$ is the pattern length and $n$ is the text length.

To check if pattern $P$ occurs:

1. Binary search for the lexicographic range where $P$ would fall
2. At each step, compare $P$ with the suffix at the current position
3. If found, all suffixes in that range start with $P$

### Memory

A suffix array for a text of length $n$ requires just $n$ integers. Using 4 bytes per integer:

$$\text{Human genome}: 3 \times 10^9 \times 4 \text{ bytes} = 12 \text{ GB}$$

This is a significant improvement over the 47 GB for a suffix tree.

### Relationship to Suffix Trees

There is an elegant connection: if you perform a **depth-first traversal** of a suffix tree, visiting children in alphabetical order, the order in which you visit the leaves gives you the suffix array.

```{=html}

<div id="viz-suffix-array" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Interactive Suffix Array</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">Enter a text to see the suffix array constructed. Search for a pattern to see binary search in action.</p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:200px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Text:</label>
    <input id="sa-text" type="text" value="abaaba" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="sa-build" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Build Suffix Array</button>
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Search pattern:</label>
    <input id="sa-pattern" type="text" placeholder="e.g. aba" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="sa-search" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#4CAF50; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Binary Search</button>
</div>
<div id="sa-table" style="overflow-x:auto; margin-bottom:10px;"></div>
<div id="sa-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; min-height:30px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
  let suffixArr = [];
  let fullText = '';

  function buildSA() {
    fullText = $('sa-text').value.toLowerCase() + '$';
    const suffixes = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < fullText.length; i++) {
      suffixes.push({pos: i, suf: fullText.substring(i)});
    }
    suffixes.sort((a, b) => a.suf < b.suf ? -1 : a.suf > b.suf ? 1 : 0);
    suffixArr = suffixes;
    renderTable([]);
    $('sa-log').innerHTML = `Suffix array for "<strong>${fullText}</strong>": [${suffixes.map(s=>s.pos).join(', ')}]`;
  }

  function renderTable(highlights) {
    let html = '<table style="width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:0.85em;">';
    html += '<tr style="background:#2196F3;color:white;"><th style="padding:6px;">Rank</th><th style="padding:6px;">SA[i]</th><th style="padding:6px;">Suffix</th><th style="padding:6px;">Status</th></tr>';
    suffixArr.forEach((s, i) => {
      const hl = highlights.find(h => h.rank === i);
      let bg = i % 2 === 0 ? '#f9f9f9' : '#fff';
      let status = '';
      if (hl) {
        if (hl.type === 'match') { bg = '#c8e6c9'; status = '<span style="color:#4CAF50;">&#10004; Match</span>'; }
        else if (hl.type === 'mid') { bg = '#fff9c4'; status = '<span style="color:#FF9800;">&#9654; Checking</span>'; }
        else if (hl.type === 'lo') { bg = '#e3f2fd'; status = '<span style="color:#2196F3;">lo</span>'; }
        else if (hl.type === 'hi') { bg = '#e3f2fd'; status = '<span style="color:#2196F3;">hi</span>'; }
        else if (hl.type === 'range') { bg = '#c8e6c9'; status = '<span style="color:#4CAF50;">&#10004; In range</span>'; }
      }
      html += `<tr style="background:${bg};"><td style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:center;">${i}</td><td style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:center;font-weight:bold;">${s.pos}</td><td style="padding:4px 8px;font-family:monospace;">${s.suf}</td><td style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:center;">${status}</td></tr>`;
    });
    html += '</table>';
    $('sa-table').innerHTML = html;
  }

  function searchSA() {
    const pattern = $('sa-pattern').value.toLowerCase();
    if (suffixArr.length === 0 || pattern.length === 0) return;

    // Binary search for left boundary
    let lo = 0, hi = suffixArr.length - 1;
    const steps = [];
    while (lo <= hi) {
      const mid = Math.floor((lo + hi) / 2);
      const suf = suffixArr[mid].suf;
      const cmp = suf.substring(0, pattern.length);
      steps.push({lo, hi, mid, cmp, result: cmp < pattern ? 'go right' : 'go left or found'});
      if (cmp < pattern) lo = mid + 1;
      else hi = mid - 1;
    }
    const left = lo;

    lo = left; hi = suffixArr.length - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
      const mid = Math.floor((lo + hi) / 2);
      const suf = suffixArr[mid].suf;
      const cmp = suf.substring(0, pattern.length);
      if (cmp > pattern) hi = mid - 1;
      else lo = mid + 1;
    }
    const right = hi;

    const highlights = [];
    if (left <= right) {
      for (let i = left; i <= right; i++) highlights.push({rank: i, type: 'range'});
    }
    renderTable(highlights);

    let logHtml = `<strong>Binary search for "${pattern}":</strong><br>`;
    steps.forEach((s, i) => {
      logHtml += `Step ${i+1}: lo=${s.lo}, hi=${s.hi}, mid=${s.mid}, compare "${s.cmp}" vs "${pattern}" &rarr; ${s.result}<br>`;
    });
    if (left <= right) {
      const positions = [];
      for (let i = left; i <= right; i++) positions.push(suffixArr[i].pos);
      logHtml += `<span style="color:#4CAF50;"><strong>Found ${right-left+1} occurrence(s) at position(s): ${positions.sort((a,b)=>a-b).join(', ')}</strong></span>`;
    } else {
      logHtml += `<span style="color:#f44336;"><strong>Pattern not found.</strong></span>`;
    }
    $('sa-log').innerHTML = logHtml;
  }

  $('sa-build').addEventListener('click', buildSA);
  $('sa-search').addEventListener('click', searchSA);
  $('sa-pattern').addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') searchSA(); });
  buildSA();
})();
</script>
```

## 10. Burrows-Wheeler Transform (BWT)

We've been building toward this: the BWT is the core data structure inside both Bowtie2 and BWA-MEM -- the two aligners you will use most often in practice.

:::{.callout-tip}
## Why not just use suffix arrays?
Suffix arrays are compact compared to suffix trees (12 GB vs. 47 GB for the human genome), but 12 GB is still too large to fit in the RAM of most workstations. The BWT achieves something remarkable: it can be compressed to **under 1 GB** while still supporting fast pattern search. This is why it -- not the suffix array directly -- became the foundation for practical alignment tools.
:::

The BWT is intimately connected to the suffix array we just studied. The sorted rotations in the BWT matrix are the same as the sorted suffixes -- the suffix array gives the starting positions, and the BWT gives the last character of each rotation. The FM index, which we will build in Section 11, exploits this connection to combine the BWT's compressibility with the suffix array's position information.

The **Burrows-Wheeler Transform** is one of the most elegant algorithms in computer science. Originally invented for data compression (1994), it turned out to be the key ingredient for modern read aligners. The BWT rearranges a string in a way that is simultaneously **compressible**, **reversible**, and **searchable**.

### Step-by-Step Construction

Given a string $T$ (with `$` appended -- recall from Section 7, `$` is a sentinel character smaller than all others, ensuring each suffix and each rotation is unique):

1. **Write all rotations** of $T$
2. **Sort** the rotations lexicographically
3. **Take the last column** -- this is the BWT

A **rotation** of a string means moving the first character to the end. So `abaaba$` → `baaba$a` → `aaba$ab` → and so on, until you cycle back to the original string.

### Worked Example

Let $T = $ `abaaba$`:

**Step 1: All rotations**

| Rotation |
|----------|
| `abaaba$` |
| `baaba$a` |
| `aaba$ab` |
| `aba$aba` |
| `ba$abaa` |
| `a$abaab` |
| `$abaaba` |

**Step 2: Sort lexicographically**

| Row | Sorted Rotation | First | Last |
|-----|----------------|-------|------|
| 0 | `$abaaba` | `$` | **a** |
| 1 | `a$abaab` | a | **b** |
| 2 | `aaba$ab` | a | **b** |
| 3 | `aba$aba` | a | **a** |
| 4 | `abaaba$` | a | **`$`** |
| 5 | `ba$abaa` | b | **a** |
| 6 | `baaba$a` | b | **a** |

**Step 3: The BWT is the last column**: `abba$aa`

### Three Remarkable Properties

#### Property 1: Compressible

The BWT tends to group identical characters together. In our example, `abba$aa` has runs of repeated characters. This makes it highly amenable to **run-length encoding** -- a key property for compression (used in bzip2).

#### Property 2: Reversible

Despite appearing to scramble the text, the BWT can be **perfectly reversed** to recover the original text. This uses the **LF mapping** property.

#### Property 3: Searchable

The BWT supports fast pattern search without decompressing -- this is what makes it useful for genomics.

### The LF Mapping Property

The **LF mapping** states: the $i$-th occurrence of character $c$ in the **Last** column (L) corresponds to the $i$-th occurrence of $c$ in the **First** column (F).

**Concrete example -- tracing one character step by step:**

Look at row 0 of our BWT matrix. The L column has `a` at row 0. This is the **1st** `a` in L (scanning top to bottom). By the LF mapping, it maps to the **1st** `a` in F -- which is at row 1.

```
         F               L
Row 0:   $  abaaba       a  ← 1st 'a' in L  ──→  maps to 1st 'a' in F (row 1)
Row 1:   a  $abaab       b
Row 2:   a  aba$ab       b
Row 3:   a  ba$aba       a  ← 2nd 'a' in L  ──→  maps to 2nd 'a' in F (row 2)
Row 4:   a  baaba$       $
Row 5:   b  a$abaa       a  ← 3rd 'a' in L  ──→  maps to 3rd 'a' in F (row 3)
Row 6:   b  aaba$a       a  ← 4th 'a' in L  ──→  maps to 4th 'a' in F (row 4)
```

Notice the pattern: the $i$-th occurrence of any character in L always maps to the $i$-th occurrence of that same character in F.

> **Why does this work?** Let's trace one example and then state the general rule.
>
> **Concrete trace:** Look at the 2nd `a` in L, which is at row 3. Row 3's rotation is `aba$aba`. The last character (L) is `a`, and the rotation that *follows* this `a` is `ba$aba` -- which is the rotation at row 3 itself. Now, the 2nd `a` in F is at row 2, whose rotation is `aaba$ab`. This rotation also sorts to the same relative position among all `a`-prefixed rotations.
>
> **The general argument in three steps:**
>
> 1. All rotations starting with `a` form a contiguous block in the sorted matrix (rows 1-4 in F). Within this block, they are sorted by what comes *after* the leading `a`.
> 2. Each `a` in L represents the character just *before* its row's rotation. The rotation that follows each of these `a`'s is a complete rotation of the original text.
> 3. Sorting these "following rotations" gives the same relative order as sorting the F-block, because it's the same set of strings. So the 1st `a` in L and the 1st `a` in F refer to the same occurrence, the 2nd to the 2nd, and so on.
>
> This holds for every character, not just `a`.

### Reversing the BWT

Using LF mapping, we can recover the original text:

1. Start at the row containing `$` in the F column (row 0)
2. Read character from L column: `a`
3. Use LF mapping to jump to the corresponding row
4. Repeat until `$` is reached
5. Read characters in reverse to get the original text

```{=html}

<div id="viz-bwt" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Interactive Burrows-Wheeler Transform</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">Enter a string to see the BWT constructed step by step. Then try reversing it and searching for patterns.</p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:200px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Text:</label>
    <input id="bwt-text" type="text" value="abaaba" maxlength="12" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>

  <button id="bwt-reverse" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#FF9800; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Reverse BWT</button>

<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Search pattern:</label>
    <input id="bwt-pattern" type="text" placeholder="e.g. aba" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="bwt-search" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#4CAF50; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Search (Backward)</button>
</div>
<div id="bwt-matrix" style="overflow-x:auto; margin-bottom:10px;"></div>
<div id="bwt-result" style="padding:6px; background:#e8f5e9; border-radius:4px; font-family:monospace; font-size:1.1em; margin-bottom:8px; min-height:24px; text-align:center;"></div>
<div id="bwt-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; min-height:30px; max-height:250px; overflow-y:auto;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
  let rotations = [], sortedRots = [], bwtStr = '', fCol = '', lCol = '';

  function buildBWT() {
    const text = $('bwt-text').value.toLowerCase() + '$';
    rotations = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
      rotations.push(text.substring(i) + text.substring(0, i));
    }
    sortedRots = rotations.slice().sort();
    fCol = sortedRots.map(r => r[0]).join('');
    lCol = sortedRots.map(r => r[r.length - 1]).join('');
    bwtStr = lCol;
    renderMatrix([]);
    $('bwt-result').innerHTML = `BWT("<strong>${text}</strong>") = <strong style="color:#2196F3; font-size:1.3em;">${bwtStr}</strong>`;
    $('bwt-log').innerHTML = `<strong>Construction:</strong> Generated ${text.length} rotations, sorted lexicographically, extracted last column.<br>First column (F): <code>${fCol}</code><br>Last column (L = BWT): <code>${lCol}</code>`;
  }

  function renderMatrix(highlights, searchRange) {
    let html = '<table style="border-collapse:collapse; font-size:0.85em; font-family:monospace; margin:0 auto;">';
    html += '<tr style="background:#2196F3; color:white;"><th style="padding:4px 6px;">Row</th><th style="padding:4px 6px;">F</th><th style="padding:4px 6px;">Rotation</th><th style="padding:4px 6px;">L</th></tr>';
    sortedRots.forEach((rot, i) => {
      const hl = highlights.find(h => h.row === i);
      let bg = i % 2 === 0 ? '#f9f9f9' : '#fff';
      let fStyle = '', lStyle = '';
      if (searchRange && i >= searchRange.lo && i <= searchRange.hi) {
        bg = '#c8e6c9';
      }
      if (hl) {
        if (hl.type === 'lf') { lStyle = 'background:#FF9800;color:white;padding:2px 4px;border-radius:3px;'; }
        if (hl.type === 'f') { fStyle = 'background:#2196F3;color:white;padding:2px 4px;border-radius:3px;'; }
      }
      const f = rot[0], l = rot[rot.length - 1];
      const middle = rot.substring(1, rot.length - 1);
      html += `<tr style="background:${bg};"><td style="padding:3px 6px;text-align:center;color:#999;">${i}</td>`;
      html += `<td style="padding:3px 6px;text-align:center;"><span style="${fStyle}">${f}</span></td>`;
      html += `<td style="padding:3px 6px;">${f}${middle}${l}</td>`;
      html += `<td style="padding:3px 6px;text-align:center;"><span style="${lStyle}">${l}</span></td></tr>`;
    });
    html += '</table>';
    $('bwt-matrix').innerHTML = html;
  }

  function reverseBWT() {
    if (bwtStr.length === 0) { buildBWT(); }
    const n = bwtStr.length;
    // Build LF mapping
    const L = bwtStr.split('');
    const F = L.slice().sort();

    // Count occurrences up to each position
    function rankAt(col, idx) {
      let count = 0;
      for (let i = 0; i < idx; i++) { if (col[i] === col[idx]) count++; }
      return count;
    }

    // LF mapping: for each position i in L, find corresponding position in F
    function lfMap(i) {
      const ch = L[i];
      const r = rankAt(L, i);
      let count = 0;
      for (let j = 0; j < n; j++) {
        if (F[j] === ch) {
          if (count === r) return j;
          count++;
        }
      }
      return 0;
    }

    // Start at the row where F = $, read L[row], follow LF mapping
    let row = F.indexOf('$');
    let recovered = '';
    let logHtml = '<strong>Reversing BWT using LF mapping:</strong><br>';
    const hlSteps = [];
    for (let step = 0; step < n - 1; step++) {
      const ch = L[row];
      recovered = ch + recovered;
      const nextRow = lfMap(row);
      logHtml += `Step ${step+1}: Row ${row}, L[${row}]='<strong>${ch}</strong>' &rarr; LF maps to Row ${nextRow}<br>`;
      row = nextRow;
    }
    logHtml += `<br><span style="color:#4CAF50;"><strong>Recovered text: ${recovered}</strong></span>`;
    $('bwt-log').innerHTML = logHtml;
    $('bwt-result').innerHTML = `Reversed BWT: <strong style="color:#4CAF50; font-size:1.3em;">${recovered}</strong>`;
  }

  function searchBWT() {
    const pattern = $('bwt-pattern').value.toLowerCase();
    if (sortedRots.length === 0 || pattern.length === 0) return;

    const n = sortedRots.length;
    // Backward search
    let lo = 0, hi = n - 1;
    let logHtml = `<strong>Backward search for "${pattern}":</strong><br>`;
    logHtml += `Starting with full range [0, ${hi}]<br>`;

    for (let i = pattern.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      const ch = pattern[i];
      // Find new lo: first row in [lo..hi] where L column = ch
      let newLo = -1, newHi = -1;

      // Count character ranks for LF mapping
      // First column positions for each character
      const charStarts = {};
      for (let j = 0; j < n; j++) {
        const fc = fCol[j];
        if (!(fc in charStarts)) charStarts[fc] = j;
      }

      if (!(ch in charStarts)) {
        logHtml += `Character '${ch}' not in text. <span style="color:#f44336;"><strong>Not found.</strong></span>`;
        $('bwt-log').innerHTML = logHtml;
        renderMatrix([], null);
        $('bwt-result').innerHTML = `<span style="color:#f44336;">Pattern "${pattern}" not found.</span>`;
        return;
      }

      // Count occurrences of ch in L[0..lo-1] and L[0..hi]
      let countBefore = 0;
      for (let j = 0; j < lo; j++) { if (lCol[j] === ch) countBefore++; }
      let countTo = 0;
      for (let j = 0; j <= hi; j++) { if (lCol[j] === ch) countTo++; }

      newLo = charStarts[ch] + countBefore;
      newHi = charStarts[ch] + countTo - 1;

      logHtml += `Processing '${ch}': C['${ch}']=${charStarts[ch]}, Occ('${ch}',${lo-1})=${countBefore}, Occ('${ch}',${hi})=${countTo} &rarr; lo=${charStarts[ch]}+${countBefore}=${newLo}, hi=${charStarts[ch]}+${countTo}&minus;1=${newHi} &rarr; [${newLo}, ${newHi}]<br>`;

      if (newLo > newHi) {
        logHtml += `<span style="color:#f44336;"><strong>Range empty. Pattern not found.</strong></span>`;
        $('bwt-log').innerHTML = logHtml;
        renderMatrix([], null);
        $('bwt-result').innerHTML = `<span style="color:#f44336;">Pattern "${pattern}" not found.</span>`;
        return;
      }
      lo = newLo;
      hi = newHi;
    }

    logHtml += `<br><span style="color:#4CAF50;"><strong>Found ${hi - lo + 1} occurrence(s) in rows ${lo} to ${hi}.</strong></span>`;
    $('bwt-log').innerHTML = logHtml;
    renderMatrix([], {lo, hi});
    $('bwt-result').innerHTML = `<span style="color:#4CAF50;"><strong>"${pattern}" found ${hi-lo+1} time(s)</strong></span>`;
  }

  $('bwt-build').addEventListener('click', buildBWT);
  $('bwt-reverse').addEventListener('click', reverseBWT);
  $('bwt-search').addEventListener('click', searchBWT);
  $('bwt-pattern').addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') searchBWT(); });
  buildBWT();
})();
</script>
```

## 11. FM Index

The BWT is powerful, but it lacks one critical piece of information: **where in the original text** do the matches occur? The BWT tells us *how many* matches exist (from the range size), but not their positions.

The **FM index** (Ferragina and Manzini, 2000) combines the BWT with auxiliary data structures to create a complete, practical search index.

### Components of the FM Index

| Component | What it stores | Size (human genome) |
|-----------|---------------|-------------------|
| **F column** | Just the counts of each character | Negligible (~16 bytes) |
| **L column (BWT)** | The Burrows-Wheeler Transform | ~750 MB (with compression) |
| **Tally/Checkpoint table** | Cumulative character counts at intervals | ~400 MB |
| **SA sample** | Every $k$-th suffix array value | ~100 MB |
| **Total** | | **~1.25 GB** |

Compare this to: raw genome (3 GB), suffix array (12 GB), suffix tree (47 GB). The FM index is remarkably compact.

### How the Tally Table Works

Instead of counting characters in L on every query (which would be $O(n)$), we precompute **checkpoints**: cumulative counts of each character at regular intervals (say, every 128 rows).

To count occurrences of character $c$ in $L[0..i]$:
1. Find the nearest checkpoint before position $i$
2. Read the precomputed count
3. Scan the few rows between the checkpoint and $i$

This gives us $O(1)$ effective lookup time.

### How Position Lookup Works

The SA sample stores suffix array values at every $k$-th position. To find the text position for a BWT match at row $i$:

1. If $SA[i]$ is stored, return it directly
2. Otherwise, follow LF mapping steps until you reach a stored position
3. Add the number of steps taken

Since we follow at most $k$ LF steps, position lookup is $O(k)$.

### The Search Algorithm

The idea is beautifully simple: we process the pattern **from right to left**, one character at a time. Why backward? Because the F column is sorted, so each character narrows our search to a contiguous block of rows. Processing right-to-left means we are always extending a prefix in the sorted rotation matrix -- which is exactly what binary search on the suffix array would do, but we achieve it in $O(1)$ per character using the precomputed tables instead of $O(\log n)$.

At each step, we maintain a range $[lo, hi]$ in the sorted rotation matrix. This range represents all rows whose corresponding suffixes start with the portion of the pattern we have processed so far. Adding one more character to the left **narrows** this range using two lookups in our precomputed tables.

The full FM index search for pattern $P[0..m-1]$:

```
Initialize: lo = 0, hi = n - 1
For i = m-1 down to 0:
    c = P[i]
    lo = C[c] + Occ(c, lo - 1)
    hi = C[c] + Occ(c, hi) - 1
    If lo > hi: pattern not found
Return: hi - lo + 1 occurrences
```

Where:
- $C[c]$ = number of characters in $T$ that are lexicographically smaller than $c$ (the start of $c$'s block in F)
- $Occ(c, i)$ = number of occurrences of $c$ in $L[0..i]$ (computed using the tally table)

> **Note**: By convention, $Occ(c, -1) = 0$ -- there are zero occurrences of any character before position 0. This handles the edge case when $lo = 0$.

### Worked Example: Searching for `"aba"` in `abaaba$`

Let's trace the algorithm on our running example. From the BWT matrix in Section 10:

| Row | F | L | SA |
|-----|---|---|----|
| 0 | `$` | `a` | 6 |
| 1 | `a` | `b` | 5 |
| 2 | `a` | `b` | 2 |
| 3 | `a` | `a` | 3 |
| 4 | `a` | `$` | 0 |
| 5 | `b` | `a` | 4 |
| 6 | `b` | `a` | 1 |

**Precomputed tables:**

- $C[\$] = 0$, $C[a] = 1$, $C[b] = 5$ &nbsp; (count of characters lexicographically smaller)
- $L = [a, b, b, a, \$, a, a]$ &nbsp; (the BWT)

**Initialize:** $lo = 0,\; hi = 6$

**Iteration 1** ($i = 2$, $c = P[2] =$ `a`, the rightmost character):

$$lo = C[a] + Occ(a, -1) = 1 + 0 = 1$$
$$hi = C[a] + Occ(a, 6) - 1 = 1 + 4 - 1 = 4$$

Range $[1, 4]$: these are the 4 rows whose suffixes start with `a`.

**Iteration 2** ($i = 1$, $c = P[1] =$ `b`):

$Occ(b, 0)$: count `b` in $L[0..0] = [a]$ → 0. &nbsp; $Occ(b, 4)$: count `b` in $L[0..4] = [a, b, b, a, \$]$ → 2.

$$lo = C[b] + Occ(b, 0) = 5 + 0 = 5$$
$$hi = C[b] + Occ(b, 4) - 1 = 5 + 2 - 1 = 6$$

Range $[5, 6]$: these are the 2 rows whose suffixes start with `ba`.

**Iteration 3** ($i = 0$, $c = P[0] =$ `a`, the leftmost character):

$Occ(a, 4)$: count `a` in $L[0..4] = [a, b, b, a, \$]$ → 2. &nbsp; $Occ(a, 6)$: count `a` in $L[0..6]$ → 4.

$$lo = C[a] + Occ(a, 4) = 1 + 2 = 3$$
$$hi = C[a] + Occ(a, 6) - 1 = 1 + 4 - 1 = 4$$

Range $[3, 4]$: **2 occurrences** found. The suffix array tells us their text positions: $SA[3] = 3$ and $SA[4] = 0$. Indeed, `aba` appears at position 0 (`abaaba$`) and position 3 (`aba$`).

> Each iteration took just two table lookups ($C$ and $Occ$) -- no character-by-character scanning. For a genome-scale FM index, searching a 100 bp pattern takes exactly 100 iterations regardless of genome size.

```{=html}

<div id="viz-fm-index" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Interactive FM Index</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">See the full FM index data structure. Search for a pattern and watch checkpoints and tally lookups highlighted step by step.</p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:200px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Text:</label>
    <input id="fm-text" type="text" value="abaaba" maxlength="14" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="fm-build" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Build FM Index</button>
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Search pattern:</label>
    <input id="fm-pattern" type="text" placeholder="e.g. aba" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="fm-search" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#4CAF50; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Search</button>
</div>
<div id="fm-components" style="display:flex; gap:15px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px;">
  <div id="fm-ctable" style="flex:1; min-width:150px;"></div>
  <div id="fm-main" style="flex:3; min-width:400px; overflow-x:auto;"></div>
</div>
<div id="fm-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; min-height:30px; max-height:250px; overflow-y:auto;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
  let fmData = {};

  function buildFM() {
    const text = $('fm-text').value.toLowerCase() + '$';
    const n = text.length;

    // Build BWT
    const rots = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) rots.push(text.substring(i) + text.substring(0, i));
    const sorted = rots.slice().sort();
    const F = sorted.map(r => r[0]);
    const L = sorted.map(r => r[r.length - 1]);

    // Build suffix array
    const suffixes = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) suffixes.push({pos: i, suf: text.substring(i)});
    suffixes.sort((a, b) => a.suf < b.suf ? -1 : a.suf > b.suf ? 1 : 0);
    const SA = suffixes.map(s => s.pos);

    // C table: number of chars lexicographically smaller
    const chars = [...new Set(text.split(''))].sort();
    const C = {};
    chars.forEach(c => {
      C[c] = 0;
      for (const ch of text) { if (ch < c) C[c]++; }
    });

    // Occ table (tally): cumulative count of each char in L[0..i]
    const Occ = {};
    chars.forEach(c => {
      Occ[c] = new Array(n).fill(0);
      let count = 0;
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (L[i] === c) count++;
        Occ[c][i] = count;
      }
    });

    fmData = {text, n, F, L, SA, C, Occ, chars, sorted};
    renderFM([]);
    $('fm-log').innerHTML = `FM index built for "<strong>${text}</strong>". Components: C table, BWT (L column), Tally (Occ), SA.`;
  }

  function renderFM(highlights, range) {
    const {n, F, L, SA, C, Occ, chars, sorted} = fmData;
    if (!n) return;

    // C table
    let cHtml = '<div style="font-size:0.8em;"><strong>C[ ] table</strong><br><em>(chars before c)</em>';
    cHtml += '<table style="border-collapse:collapse;margin-top:4px;">';
    chars.forEach(c => {
      cHtml += `<tr><td style="padding:2px 6px;font-family:monospace;font-weight:bold;border:1px solid #ddd;">${c === '$' ? '$' : c}</td><td style="padding:2px 6px;text-align:center;border:1px solid #ddd;">${C[c]}</td></tr>`;
    });
    cHtml += '</table></div>';
    $('fm-ctable').innerHTML = cHtml;

    // Main table
    let html = '<table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-size:0.8em;font-family:monospace;width:100%;">';
    html += '<tr style="background:#2196F3;color:white;"><th style="padding:3px 4px;">i</th><th style="padding:3px 4px;">SA</th><th style="padding:3px 4px;">F</th><th style="padding:3px 4px;">L</th>';
    chars.forEach(c => { html += `<th style="padding:3px 4px;">Occ(${c === '$' ? '$' : c})</th>`; });
    html += '</tr>';

    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      const hl = highlights.find(h => h.row === i);
      const inRange = range && i >= range.lo && i <= range.hi;
      let bg = i % 2 === 0 ? '#f9f9f9' : '#fff';
      if (inRange) bg = '#c8e6c9';
      if (hl && hl.type === 'active') bg = '#fff9c4';
      html += `<tr style="background:${bg};">`;
      html += `<td style="padding:2px 4px;text-align:center;color:#999;border:1px solid #eee;">${i}</td>`;
      html += `<td style="padding:2px 4px;text-align:center;border:1px solid #eee;">${SA[i]}</td>`;
      html += `<td style="padding:2px 4px;text-align:center;font-weight:bold;border:1px solid #eee;color:#1565C0;">${F[i]}</td>`;
      html += `<td style="padding:2px 4px;text-align:center;font-weight:bold;border:1px solid #eee;color:#c62828;">${L[i]}</td>`;
      chars.forEach(c => {
        html += `<td style="padding:2px 4px;text-align:center;border:1px solid #eee;">${Occ[c][i]}</td>`;
      });
      html += '</tr>';
    }
    html += '</table>';
    $('fm-main').innerHTML = html;
  }

  function searchFM() {
    const pattern = $('fm-pattern').value.toLowerCase();
    const {n, F, L, SA, C, Occ, chars} = fmData;
    if (!n || pattern.length === 0) return;

    let lo = 0, hi = n - 1;
    let logHtml = `<strong>FM index search for "${pattern}"</strong> (backward, right to left):<br>`;
    logHtml += `Initial range: [${lo}, ${hi}]<br><br>`;

    for (let i = pattern.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      const c = pattern[i];
      if (!(c in C)) {
        logHtml += `Character '${c}' not in alphabet. <span style="color:#f44336;"><strong>Not found.</strong></span>`;
        $('fm-log').innerHTML = logHtml;
        renderFM([], null);
        return;
      }
      const occLo = lo > 0 ? Occ[c][lo - 1] : 0;
      const occHi = Occ[c][hi];
      const newLo = C[c] + occLo;
      const newHi = C[c] + occHi - 1;

      logHtml += `<strong>Step: char '${c}' (position ${i})</strong><br>`;
      logHtml += `&nbsp;&nbsp;C['${c}'] = ${C[c]}<br>`;
      logHtml += `&nbsp;&nbsp;Occ('${c}', ${lo > 0 ? lo-1 : -1}) = ${occLo}<br>`;
      logHtml += `&nbsp;&nbsp;Occ('${c}', ${hi}) = ${occHi}<br>`;
      logHtml += `&nbsp;&nbsp;new lo = ${C[c]} + ${occLo} = ${newLo}<br>`;
      logHtml += `&nbsp;&nbsp;new hi = ${C[c]} + ${occHi} - 1 = ${newHi}<br>`;

      if (newLo > newHi) {
        logHtml += `<span style="color:#f44336;"><strong>Range empty. Pattern not found.</strong></span>`;
        $('fm-log').innerHTML = logHtml;
        renderFM([], null);
        return;
      }
      lo = newLo;
      hi = newHi;
      logHtml += `&nbsp;&nbsp;Range: [${lo}, ${hi}]<br><br>`;
    }

    const positions = [];
    for (let i = lo; i <= hi; i++) positions.push(SA[i]);
    positions.sort((a, b) => a - b);

    logHtml += `<span style="color:#4CAF50;"><strong>Found ${hi - lo + 1} occurrence(s) at text position(s): ${positions.join(', ')}</strong></span>`;
    $('fm-log').innerHTML = logHtml;
    renderFM([], {lo, hi});
  }

  $('fm-build').addEventListener('click', buildFM);
  $('fm-search').addEventListener('click', searchFM);
  $('fm-pattern').addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') searchFM(); });
  buildFM();
})();
</script>
```

## 12. Bowtie2 Algorithm

Now that we understand the FM index, let's see how modern read aligners use it. [Bowtie2](http://bowtie-bio.sourceforge.net/bowtie2/index.shtml) (Langmead & Salzberg, 2012) is one of the most widely used short-read aligners.

### Overview

Bowtie2 uses a **seed-and-extend** strategy:

1. **Seed**: Extract short substrings from the read and find exact matches using the FM index
2. **Extend**: Use dynamic programming to extend seeds into full alignments

### How Bowtie2 Uses the FM Index for Seeding

Each seed is looked up in the FM index using the **backward search** from Section 11. The algorithm processes the seed characters from right to left, narrowing the $[lo, hi]$ range at each step. If the range is non-empty at the end, the seed has exact matches in the reference, and the suffix array sample provides their genomic positions.

Bowtie2 also allows a small number of mismatches within seeds. It achieves this by trying multiple "seed variants" -- backtracking during the FM index search to substitute alternative characters at certain positions. This is more expensive than pure exact matching but catches seeds that differ from the reference by one or two bases.

### Seed Extraction

Bowtie2 extracts seeds of configurable length (default: 22 bp for end-to-end mode) from the read. Seeds can be extracted at regular intervals along the read.

For a 100 bp read with seed length 22 and interval 11:

```
Read:   ACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGT...
Seed 1: ACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTAC (pos 0-21)
Seed 2:            TACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTA (pos 11-32)
Seed 3:                       CGTACGTACGTACGTACGTAC (pos 22-43)
...
```

### Worked Example: Aligning a Read with a SNP

Consider a 50 bp read that has a single G→A SNP at position 25:

```
Reference: ...ACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTAC...
Read:       ACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTAACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTAC
                                    ^
                                   SNP (G→A at pos 25)
```

Bowtie2 extracts seeds (length 22, interval 11):

```
Seed 1: ACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACG  (pos 0-21)  → exact FM index match ✓
Seed 2: TACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACG (pos 11-32)  → contains SNP, no exact match ✗
Seed 3: ACGTAACGTACGTACGTACGTACG (pos 22-43)  → contains SNP, no exact match ✗
```

Seed 1 hits the reference. Bowtie2 uses that hit as an **anchor** and extends the alignment in both directions using dynamic programming. The extension discovers the G→A mismatch at position 25 and produces a full alignment with one penalty.

### Scoring Model

Bowtie2 uses a configurable scoring model:

| Event | Default Score |
|-------|--------------|
| Match | 0 (no bonus in end-to-end mode) |
| Mismatch | -6 |
| Gap open | -5 |
| Gap extend | -3 |
| Read gap open | -5 |
| Read gap extend | -3 |

> **Why does a match score 0?** Bowtie2 uses a **penalty-based** scoring system in end-to-end mode, where the maximum possible score is 0 (a perfect match with no mismatches or gaps). Every error subtracts from this score. This is different from the reward-based scoring you may be used to from Smith-Waterman. In **local** mode, matches do receive a bonus (+2 by default).

### Alignment Modes

| Mode | Description | Use when |
|------|-------------|----------|
| **End-to-end** | Align entire read, penalize unaligned ends | Standard short-read alignment |
| **Local** | Allow soft-clipping of read ends | Reads may have adapter contamination |

### Handling Multimapping and MAPQ

When a read maps to multiple genomic locations, Bowtie2 assigns a **mapping quality (MAPQ)** score reflecting confidence that the reported position is correct. MAPQ is a Phred-scaled probability: $MAPQ = -10 \log_{10}(P_{\text{wrong}})$. A MAPQ of 0 means the read maps equally well to multiple locations; a MAPQ of 42 (Bowtie2's maximum) means high confidence in a unique placement. Downstream tools like variant callers use MAPQ to weight or filter alignments.

### Parameter Tuning Guide

| Parameter | Default | When to change |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| `--seed-len` (`-L`) | 22 | Lower (e.g., 16-20) for divergent references or high mutation rates; higher (e.g., 28-32) to increase speed at the cost of sensitivity |
| `--seed-interval` (`-i`) | f(read length) | Lower for higher sensitivity, higher for speed |
| `--local` | off | Use when reads may contain adapter sequence or when you want soft-clipping |
| `-N` | 0 | Set to 1 to allow one mismatch in seeds (slower but more sensitive) |
| `-k` | 1 (best) | Increase to report multiple alignments (e.g., `-k 10` for multimapping analysis) |

### Key Features

- **FM index** for memory-efficient seed finding
- **Supports gapped alignment** (unlike Bowtie1)
- **Multiple alignment modes** (best, all valid, up to $k$)
- **Paired-end aware** -- uses mate pair information to improve mapping
- **Fast for short reads** -- optimized for reads up to ~250 bp

---

## 13. BWA-MEM Algorithm

[BWA-MEM](https://github.com/lh3/bwa) (Li, 2013) is the other dominant short-read aligner. It also uses the FM index but with a different seeding strategy.

### Maximal Exact Matches (MEMs)

Instead of fixed-length seeds, BWA-MEM finds **Maximal Exact Matches (MEMs)**: the longest substrings of the read that match the reference exactly.

A MEM is **maximal** in the sense that it cannot be extended in either direction without introducing a mismatch.

### How MEMs Are Found Using the FM Index

BWA-MEM finds MEMs by extending the FM index backward search until the match range becomes empty. Starting at each position $i$ in the read:

1. Begin a backward search from position $i$, processing characters leftward
2. At each step, the $[lo, hi]$ range narrows. Track the range size
3. When the range becomes empty (no matches), stop -- the longest match ending at $i$ was the step just before the range emptied
4. Then extend rightward from position $i$ as well, checking if the match can grow
5. The resulting longest bidirectional exact match is a MEM

This is more efficient than it sounds: BWA-MEM processes all positions in a single sweep using the FM index, reusing range information from adjacent positions.

### Super-Maximal Exact Matches (SMEMs)

BWA-MEM further refines MEMs into **SMEMs**: MEMs that are not contained within any longer MEM. An SMEM is the longest exact match covering each read position.

Consider aligning a read against a reference where there is a single SNP (T→G) at read position 12:

```
Reference: ACGTACGTACGT T CGTACGTAC
Read:      ACGTACGTACGT G CGTACGTAC
           |           |           |
           pos 0       pos 12      pos 21

SMEM 1: ACGTACGTACGT  (read pos 0-11,  length 12) — exact match left of SNP
SMEM 2: CGTACGTAC     (read pos 13-21, length 9)  — exact match right of SNP
```

Neither SMEM can be extended without hitting the mismatch at position 12. Together, they cover the entire read except the SNP position -- giving BWA-MEM two anchor points for alignment.

### Chaining

Once SMEMs are found, BWA-MEM groups them into **chains**: sets of SMEMs that are **collinear** (they appear in the same order and with consistent spacing in both the read and the reference).

```
Read:        [---SMEM1---]---[--SMEM2--]------[---SMEM3---]
Reference:   [---SMEM1---]---[--SMEM2--]------[---SMEM3---]
                ↑ same order, consistent gaps → forms one chain

Read:        [---SMEM1---]---[--SMEM2--]
Reference:       [--SMEM2--]---[---SMEM1---]
                ↑ reversed order → different chains (possible inversion)
```

Chaining is critical because it distinguishes true alignments from spurious seed hits. A chain of collinear SMEMs strongly suggests a real genomic origin, while isolated seeds may be coincidental matches in repetitive regions.

### The BWA-MEM Pipeline

1. **SMEM finding**: Use FM index to find all SMEMs (minimum length: 19 bp by default)
2. **Re-seeding**: For very long SMEMs (> 28 bp), re-seed with shorter fragments to handle mismatches within long matching regions
3. **Chaining**: Group SMEMs that are collinear (consistent order and spacing) into chains
4. **Smith-Waterman**: Extend the best chains using banded Smith-Waterman dynamic programming to produce full alignments with gaps and mismatches
5. **Pairing**: For paired-end reads, resolve pairs using insert-size distribution

### Handling Repetitive Regions

Repetitive sequences (e.g., Alu elements, LINE-1, centromeric repeats) are a major challenge. A seed from a repetitive region may match thousands of positions. BWA-MEM handles this by:

- **Dropping overrepresented seeds**: If an SMEM matches more than 500 positions (configurable with `-c`), BWA-MEM discards it and relies on neighboring, more specific seeds
- **Re-seeding**: Long SMEMs in repetitive regions are broken into shorter fragments that may be more specific
- **MAPQ scoring**: Reads in repetitive regions receive low MAPQ scores, flagging uncertainty for downstream analysis

### Key Features

- **Flexible read length**: Works well from 70 bp to 1 Mbp
- **Split-read alignment**: Can align chimeric reads (important for structural variants)
- **Better for longer reads**: The MEM seeding strategy scales well with read length
- **Robust to errors**: Re-seeding handles higher error rates

---

## 14. Bowtie2 vs. BWA-MEM Comparison

Both tools use the FM index at their core, but they differ in strategy and strengths.

### Side-by-Side Comparison

| Feature | Bowtie2 | BWA-MEM |
|---------|---------|---------|
| **Index** | FM index (BWT) | FM index (BWT) |
| **Seeding** | Fixed-length extracted seeds | Maximal Exact Matches (MEMs) |
| **Seed length** | Configurable (default 22) | Variable (adaptive) |
| **Extension** | Dynamic programming | Banded Smith-Waterman |
| **Optimal read length** | 50-250 bp | 70 bp - 1 Mbp |
| **Gapped alignment** | Yes | Yes |
| **Split-read** | Limited | Yes |
| **Speed (short reads)** | Very fast | Fast |
| **Speed (long reads)** | Slower | Better |
| **Memory** | ~3.2 GB (human) | ~5.4 GB (human) |
| **Runtime (30x human WGS)** | ~2-4 hours | ~2-6 hours |

### When to Use Which

| Scenario | Recommended Tool |
|----------|-----------------|
| Short Illumina reads (< 250 bp), standard WGS/WES | Either works well |
| RNA-seq (with splice-aware aligner like HISAT2) | HISAT2 (Bowtie2 family) |
| Longer reads (PacBio HiFi, Nanopore) | BWA-MEM (or minimap2) |
| Structural variant detection | BWA-MEM |
| ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq | Bowtie2 |
| Very large cohort studies (speed critical) | Bowtie2 |
| Mixed read lengths | BWA-MEM |

### Practical Recommendations

> **For most standard Illumina sequencing projects**, BWA-MEM is the default choice recommended by the GATK Best Practices pipeline. Its MEM-based seeding is robust and efficient across a wide range of read lengths.

> **For specialized applications** like ChIP-seq peak calling, Bowtie2's scoring model and reporting options (e.g., reporting only unique alignments) may be preferable.

```{=html}
<div id="viz-comparison" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Bowtie2 vs. BWA-MEM: Seeding Strategy Comparison</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">See how the same read is processed differently by each algorithm's seeding approach.<br><em>Note: This is a simplified visualization. Real MEMs are found by matching against a reference genome using the FM index. Here, we approximate MEMs as contiguous non-N regions to illustrate the concept of variable-length vs. fixed-length seeds.</em></p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:250px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Read sequence:</label>
    <input id="cmp-read" type="text" value="ACGTACGTNNCGTACGTAC" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; text-transform:uppercase; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <div>
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Bowtie2 seed length:</label>
    <input id="cmp-seedlen" type="number" value="5" min="3" max="15" style="width:70px; padding:6px; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <div>
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Min MEM length:</label>
    <input id="cmp-memlen" type="number" value="4" min="2" max="10" style="width:70px; padding:6px; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="cmp-run" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Compare</button>
</div>

<div style="display:flex; gap:20px; flex-wrap:wrap;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:380px;">
    <div style="text-align:center; font-weight:bold; color:#1565C0; margin-bottom:6px;">Bowtie2 (Fixed Seeds)</div>
    <svg id="cmp-bt2" width="100%" height="120" style="border:1px solid #e3f2fd; border-radius:4px; background:#f5f9ff;"></svg>
  </div>
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:380px;">
    <div style="text-align:center; font-weight:bold; color:#2E7D32; margin-bottom:6px;">BWA-MEM (MEMs)</div>
    <svg id="cmp-bwa" width="100%" height="120" style="border:1px solid #e8f5e9; border-radius:4px; background:#f5fff5;"></svg>
  </div>
</div>
<div id="cmp-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; margin-top:8px; min-height:30px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
  const colors = ['#2196F3','#4CAF50','#FF9800','#9C27B0','#f44336','#00BCD4','#795548','#E91E63'];

  function run() {
    const read = $('cmp-read').value.toUpperCase();
    const seedLen = parseInt($('cmp-seedlen').value);
    const minMEM = parseInt($('cmp-memlen').value);
    const n = read.length;

    // Bowtie2-style: fixed seeds at regular intervals
    const seeds = [];
    const interval = Math.max(1, Math.floor(seedLen / 2));
    for (let i = 0; i <= n - seedLen; i += interval) {
      seeds.push({start: i, end: i + seedLen, seq: read.substring(i, i + seedLen)});
    }

    // BWA-MEM-style: MEMs simulated as runs of non-N characters.
    // Note: Real MEMs are found by matching against a reference genome via the FM index.
    // Here we approximate to illustrate the concept of variable-length seeds.
    const mems = [];
    let start = -1;
    for (let i = 0; i <= n; i++) {
      if (i < n && read[i] !== 'N') {
        if (start < 0) start = i;
      } else {
        if (start >= 0 && (i - start) >= minMEM) {
          mems.push({start, end: i, seq: read.substring(start, i)});
        }
        start = -1;
      }
    }

    // Render Bowtie2
    const svg1 = $('cmp-bt2');
    const w1 = svg1.clientWidth || 400;
    const charW = Math.min(20, (w1 - 40) / n);
    const offsetX = (w1 - charW * n) / 2;
    let html1 = '';
    // Read
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      html1 += `<text x="${offsetX + i * charW + charW/2}" y="25" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-family="monospace" fill="#333">${read[i]}</text>`;
    }
    // Seeds
    seeds.forEach((s, idx) => {
      const c = colors[idx % colors.length];
      const x = offsetX + s.start * charW;
      const w = (s.end - s.start) * charW;
      const y = 40 + (idx % 3) * 24;
      html1 += `<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${w}" height="18" fill="${c}" opacity="0.7" rx="3"/>`;
      html1 += `<text x="${x + w/2}" y="${y + 13}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="white" font-weight="bold">${s.seq}</text>`;
    });
    svg1.innerHTML = html1;

    // Render BWA-MEM
    const svg2 = $('cmp-bwa');
    const w2 = svg2.clientWidth || 400;
    const charW2 = Math.min(20, (w2 - 40) / n);
    const offsetX2 = (w2 - charW2 * n) / 2;
    let html2 = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      html2 += `<text x="${offsetX2 + i * charW2 + charW2/2}" y="25" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-family="monospace" fill="#333">${read[i]}</text>`;
    }
    mems.forEach((m, idx) => {
      const c = colors[idx % colors.length];
      const x = offsetX2 + m.start * charW2;
      const w = (m.end - m.start) * charW2;
      const y = 45 + (idx % 2) * 28;
      html2 += `<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${w}" height="20" fill="${c}" opacity="0.7" rx="3"/>`;
      html2 += `<text x="${x + w/2}" y="${y + 14}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="white" font-weight="bold">${m.seq}</text>`;
    });
    svg2.innerHTML = html2;

    $('cmp-log').innerHTML = `<strong>Bowtie2:</strong> ${seeds.length} fixed-length seeds (${seedLen} bp each, interval ${interval}). <strong>BWA-MEM:</strong> ${mems.length} MEM(s) (min length ${minMEM}, variable length). BWA-MEM seeds adapt to the sequence, producing fewer but longer matches.`;
  }

  $('cmp-run').addEventListener('click', run);
  run();
})();
</script>
```

## Summary

We have traced a remarkable intellectual journey:

| Data Structure / Tool | Space | Query Time | Key Idea |
|----------------------|-------|------------|----------|
| Brute force | O(1) | O(mn) per read | Compare everywhere |
| Substring index | O(nL) | O(L + hits) | Fixed-length k-mers |
| Hash table | O(n) | O(1) average | Direct address via hash |
| **BLAST** | **O(query)** | **O(db) scan** | **Word lookup table + extend** |
| Trie | O(n L) | O(m) | Tree-structured prefix lookup |
| Suffix trie | O(n^2) | O(m) | All suffixes in a trie |
| Suffix tree | O(n) | O(m) | Collapsed suffix trie |
| Suffix array | O(n) | O(m log n) | Sorted suffix positions |
| **FM index** | **O(n)** compressed | **O(m)** | **BWT + auxiliary tables** |

BLAST uses hash-table-based word lookup to speed up homology search against large databases. The FM index goes further: compact storage, fast search, and exact matches in time proportional to the pattern length alone. This is why both Bowtie2 and BWA-MEM -- the tools you will use most often for read alignment -- are built on top of the FM index rather than BLAST-style lookup tables.

:::{.callout-important}
## The Key Lesson
In computational biology, the right data structure can make the difference between an analysis that takes centuries and one that takes minutes. Algorithmic thinking is not a luxury -- it is a necessity.
:::
